IlluminaraI won't tell you it's talking. I haven't seen enough to say so, and you would be right not to believe me if I did. I'd like your dock-clock traffic log, Dr. Brannock's flare record, the specifications of every detector, and the room until the evening session.

Teodora VanceThe council sits at eighteen hundred. At eighteen hundred I put the evacuation to a vote.

IlluminaraThen I'll bring you something you can test before you vote.

Vance looked at the clock and then at her. Curiosity did not soften her face; it made the responsibility in it more exact.

Teodora VanceTest it with what? We have sixty-nine hours and fifty-one minutes.

02 · Nine Years of Margins

Ring observatory, Brannock's office · Day 1, 09:30

Ilse Brannock kept the flare record in a ledger as well as on the network, because the ledger could not be edited by anyone who disliked it. Nine years of the Wick filled it, night by night, in a small upright hand with questions in the margins. A few were underlined twice.

Ilse BrannockYou're the ice woman with the thermal models.

IlluminaraToday I'm the ice woman who read your flare record. It's very clean. Who keeps it?

Ilse BrannockI do. Nobody else wanted to. A flare is a flare.

IlluminaraYou don't think so.

Ilse put a hand flat on the ledger as one might on a sleeping animal.

Ilse BrannockI showed this to two people. One laughed, kindly, which was worse. I said the Wick grows louder when we do. After every busy evening the next burst is larger by about the same fraction. A star's flares don't care about our trade. I knew how it sounded, so I stopped saying it.

IlluminaraAnd the timing?

Ilse BrannockAlways in a gap. I called it the small hours because that was the gap we kept giving it.

Illuminara laid the traffic log over the flare record on the glass table. The observatory clock and dock clock were three minutes apart. Nobody had held the records together because the exchange net carried private trade.

She slid one trace by three minutes. The bright marks dropped into the troughs of the traffic like coins into a purse.

Ilse BrannockFour-oh-five. Shift change. The ring goes quiet for twenty minutes while the crews swap.

IlluminaraThe size follows the loudness before the gap. The timing follows the gap itself. If there is an intention here, the least extravagant account is not anger. It is turn-taking: something raising its voice over a crowd, then waiting not to be overwritten. But the same trace could still come from a rotating spot, a precursor that suppresses our band, or chance.

Ilse BrannockSay what you want to do.

IlluminaraMove the gap. Fill four-oh-five with ordinary traffic, open a new gap at seven, and write every prediction before we touch the switches.

Ilse BrannockThe exchange monitor shares the band. A precursor could fool it.

IlluminaraWhat does not share it?

Ilse BrannockThe old bolometric plate. Hard wire, separate clock, nothing in the exchange band. Rourke wanted it scrapped.

IlluminaraThen it stays. And you present the test. I will not borrow nine years of your listening and call it my discovery.

Ilse looked at the double-underlined question in her ledger. Hope is not evidence, Illuminara thought. But shame can hide evidence for years if nobody makes room for the person carrying it.

Ilse BrannockI will present it if the envelope contains the ways I may be wrong.

IlluminaraPut them first.

03 · The Case for Flight

Council chamber · Day 1, 18:00

Vance opened the session by reading the clock aloud: fifty-nine hours, ten minutes. Then she gave the floor to Rourke, who stood with his hands behind him, like a man giving evidence in a trial he hoped to lose.

Pell RourkeThe dangerous dawn alignment on Day Four, ordinary traffic, one point three of rating. Our two requested test gaps may draw smaller responses before it. If they do, that is new behavior, not the seventh and eighth members of the old sequence. It may strengthen the case for turn-taking, or mean the experiment itself is increasing the hazard.

Teodora VanceThat's the case for flight, and I will make it myself so nobody thinks I haven't. Evacuations fail when they start late. A star that changes because we ask it to is not automatically safer than a star that does not.

Gideon Farrow rose from the guild benches. He was round and beautifully dressed and had been counting something in his head for the whole session.

Gideon FarrowWho pays if we flee from a weather event? The ice is my guild's wages and the ring's drinking water. It can't be that nobody may ask whether the star is just a star.

Teodora VanceNobody has forbidden it. Dr. Brannock?

Ilse stood. Her hands were steady on the lectern, and Illuminara, three rows back, saw her find the notes she had meant not to need.

Ilse BrannockI have nine years of flares, three instruments and three clocks. The timing sits in the quiet of our traffic, and the size follows the loudness before it. I have three rivals: a spot rotating every twenty-four-point-one hours, a lull caused by a precursor rather than chosen by us, and chance.

Teodora VanceHow much chance?

Ilse BrannockI preserved the clustering in the nine-year record and shuffled ten thousand pairs of gaps with the same widths and traffic levels. Seven pairs caught bursts in both timing windows and both amplitude bands. Seven in ten thousand is not zero. It is also not an argument I would throw away.

Dov AchterbergA calculation built from the same ledger that suggested the question. And your windows are fifty minutes wide.

Ilse BrannockYes. Which is why the spot and precursor predictions are sealed beside ours. If the spot fires at the old hour, we lose. If the exchange band fails while the independent plate stays quiet, we lose. If one requested result misses, we write miss before we explain anything.

IlluminaraAt four-oh-five tomorrow we fill the usual gap with ordinary traffic. At seven we pause the exchange net for twenty-two minutes. The independent plate remains live. We repeat with a shorter gap after the next dusk peak. The council writes the stop conditions.

Gideon FarrowWhat does the pause cost my traders?

IlluminaraTell the room what they need to keep.

Gideon FarrowThe settlement hour. Move around it and I will sell the test to the guild. I won't sell a permanent blackout.

Dov AchterbergNor should he. A scheduled silence is a scheduled vulnerability. Medical calls, collision alarms, smugglers who know when nobody is looking. If the proposed cure requires fourteen thousand people to become deaf on a timetable, I prefer the ferries.

Illuminara turned toward him rather than back to the lectern.

IlluminaraThen the test must preserve an emergency carrier outside the crowded band, and any lasting arrangement must be movable. Nadim, can that be done without contaminating the plate?

Nadim OyelaranA narrow red channel, hard-limited to alarms and medical speech. The plate won't see it. For a lasting window, the Chair could choose within a ninety-minute band and announce it fifteen minutes ahead.

Teodora VanceNoted. My cancel line: any requested burst over nine-tenths, any burst outside both registered windows, any failure of the independent plate, or any failure of the red channel. The ferries are fuelled tonight and manifests cut. A trigger starts loading within one hour; completing it still takes twenty-six. Nobody edits that sentence afterward.

04 · The Gap Moves

Communications office, exchange net · Day 2, 06:52

At four-oh-five the old gap had been filled, and the Wick had said nothing. The exchange band stayed clean; so did the independent bolometric plate. Ilse had been awake since the previous morning and sat very straight in a chair she had not chosen.

Nadim OyelaranSealed envelope is in the council log. Rotation said four-oh-five, which did not happen. Precursor said the exchange band would fail there while the plate remained quiet, which did not happen. Turn-taking says seven, within twenty-five minutes, between half and seven-tenths of rating.

At seven the exchange net went quiet. Kitchens went on, ferries stayed fuelled, and the red emergency carrier whispered with two medical calls and one collision alarm. The trading floor stopped for twenty-two minutes as fourteen thousand people agreed to leave a space.

The hard-wired plate drew a flat line, then a flat line, and then a sharp stroke at seven-oh-two. The network monitor followed a fraction later. The long shoulder on the decay was the mark Ilse had drawn in her ledger for nine years.

Ilse BrannockFifty-eight hundredths on the plate.

Nadim OyelaranInside timing and amplitude. Red channel never dropped.

Nobody cheered. Illuminara held Ilse's elbow only after the older woman reached for her.

Ilse BrannockOne.

IlluminaraOne.

The second requested gap came at twenty-two thirty on the same day, after a smaller dusk peak. A weak rise appeared on the exchange monitor eleven minutes before the pause. Dov, watching from the council feed, called it a precursor. The hard-wired plate stayed level.

At twenty-two thirty-six the Wick flared. The registered amplitude band ended at forty hundredths. The plate climbed to forty-one.

Dov AchterbergOutside the envelope.

Ilse BrannockBy one hundredth. It is a miss.

Nadim OyelaranThe early rise was our own carrier leaking into the exchange monitor. It is absent from the plate. That defeats the precursor claim, but it does not put the amplitude back inside the envelope.

Pell RourkeAnd two requested responses in sixteen hours are faster than the old forty-four-hour background. If we are causing them, that matters more than whether we have taught the sun manners.

Illuminara studied the two traces and did not rescue her prediction.

IlluminaraRecord the timing hit, the amplitude miss, the failed precursor rival and the faster cadence. Then stop opening gaps until the council decides what the faster cadence means.

Ilse BrannockYou wanted a second night.

IlluminaraI wanted an answer that could tell us no. This one has.

05 · Forty Hours

Council chamber · Day 2, 23:10

Clock hour forty found the chamber full. On the wall were four lines, none softened: OLD-GAP SILENCE; FIRST REQUEST HIT; SECOND REQUEST TIMING HIT / AMPLITUDE MISS; REQUESTED CADENCE FASTER THAN BACKGROUND.

Teodora VanceNobody in this room gets to call that two clean predictions. Dr. Brannock, what survives?

Ilse BrannockThe rotating-spot prediction failed at four-oh-five. The precursor prediction failed on the independent plate. In ten thousand paired shuffles, seven matched both timing and amplitude; ours matched both timings but only one amplitude. The data still prefers schedule-response. It does not prove a mind, and the faster cadence may be a cost of asking.

Dov AchterbergThen stop asking and load the ferries. The experiment changed the thing we feared.

Pell RourkeOr exposed that it was already waiting for gaps we happened to give it. The Day Four burst remains the dangerous one. With the dusk cap and the parasol turned before dawn, my median is eight-tenths. Without them, one point three.

Dov AchterbergMedian. Your upper edge?

Pell RourkeNine-tenths. At the cancel line.

The two numbers stayed between them. Vance looked not at Illuminara but at Ilse.

Teodora VanceIf we stay, what do you ask the Wick to do?

Ilse BrannockNothing beyond what the dangerous burst may do anyway. One bounded silence at dawn, three pulses from our cutter, then no second request. If the flare comes in the window and under the line, we learn whether leaving room changes the load. If not, the manifests are already cut.

Gideon FarrowThe dusk cap costs the guild its best settlement of the quarter. We will take it once. Not daily, and not without the loss entered beside the science.

Dov AchterbergAnd no fixed daily blackout. The red channel stays open. Any later window moves inside the ninety-minute band, fifteen minutes' notice, renewed by vote each day. Security may cancel it without your permission.

Nadim OyelaranI can enforce that in hardware. Trade carrier dark; red carrier live; plate independent. Six signatures to change it.

IlluminaraThat is better than what I brought you.

Teodora VanceIt is safer because the people paying for it changed it.

Vance kept one hand on the written cancel line.

Teodora VanceThe ferries stay fuelled. Loading starts within one hour if the plate crosses nine-tenths, the flare leaves the window, the red carrier fails, or security calls the silence unsafe. Anyone may take a berth now. We attempt one bounded exchange at dawn. Dov's moving-window amendment and Farrow's cost ledger are part of the motion.

The vote passed seven to four, not nine to two. Dov voted no. His amendment passed eleven to zero.

Afterward the reply was designed in the communications office. Nadim had the forty-metre ice-cutting array. Ilse had her ledger open to the rising edge of the first requested flare.

Nadim OyelaranI can give it a beam. I can't tell you it will see it.

Ilse BrannockThree pulses on the rhythm of its own rise. Then silence for as long as the pulses took. Heard, and your turn.

IlluminaraNo claim about what it means.

Ilse BrannockNo. Only a courtesy we can withdraw.

06 · A Turn at Four-Oh-Five

Calloway Reach, communications office and Rakel Quay · Day 4, 04:05

Under ordinary traffic the dangerous burst had been forecast at one point three of parasol rating. Farrow's dusk cap cost the guild its best evening of the quarter. Turning the parasol cost a month's thruster propellant and left Rakel Quay outside its full shadow. Rourke's registered range was seven-tenths to nine-tenths. Nine-tenths remained the line.

The Chair chose four-oh-five from the ninety-minute band and announced it fifteen minutes before. The red carrier stayed live. In the communications office Nadim held the beam trigger. On Rakel Quay his sister Kemi and two riggers waited beside the relay-mast breakers, because the model said the exposed masts would take the first side-load.

Kemi OyelaranRakel ready. You owe me two masts if your polite sun sneezes.

Nadim OyelaranPut them on Farrow's ledger.

Gideon FarrowThey are already there.

At four-oh-five Nadim sent three pulses. The trade band remained silent afterward. A medical call crossed the red carrier from nursery six; a child had swallowed a button. The silence did not make the ring helpless.

Four minutes passed.

The independent plate climbed.

Pell RourkePoint six. Point seven-two. Parasol taking thirty-one percent.

A second shoulder rose under the first.

Teodora VanceRead the plate, not the model.

Pell RourkePoint eight-six.

At Rakel, the first mast began to arc. Kemi cut its breaker before the automatic relay understood what was happening. The mast folded across an empty loading rail. The second leaned toward a fuel line.

Kemi OyelaranLosing west two. Clearing the line now.

She drove the quay tug into the mast's lower brace. Metal went down away from the fuel line, taking the tug's manipulator arm with it.

Nadim OyelaranKemi?

Kemi OyelaranStill expensive.

The plate touched eighty-nine hundredths. For twelve seconds its uncertainty band crossed the line, though the central reading did not.

Teodora VanceRourke.

Pell RourkeCentral reading below nine. Structure stable. My recommendation is hold, Chair. Your line says over, not near.

Vance's finger rested on the loading order. She could have called uncertainty a trigger. Nobody would have blamed her.

Teodora VanceHold. Kemi has the quay. Red carrier is live. If the central plate rises one hundredth, load.

It did not. The long shoulder fell through eight-tenths, then seven. The parasol held. Rakel lost two relay masts and one tug arm; no one was hurt.

In the decay, with Nadim's array still silent and the ring keeping the space it had promised, the independent plate drew three small steps.

Ilse BrannockThree. I have nine years and it has never made three.

IlluminaraDon't read it yet. We don't know that it's a reply.

Ilse BrannockNo. We know only that it happened after our three.

They did not repeat the request that night. The next day the council authorized one movable window, with the red channel and security veto intact, and required a fresh vote every seven days. Farrow entered the lost settlement, two masts, a tug arm and a month of propellant in the same ledger as the avoided evacuation. Dov signed the safety protocol and wrote beneath his name that he still believed they should leave.

Teodora VanceHe is allowed to be wrong in the record, if he is wrong.

IlluminaraSo are we.

Ilse closed her ledger, opened it again, and wrote on the next clean line in her small upright hand: Four-oh-five. We stopped. It knocked.

Teodora VanceNobody in this room gets to call that two clean predictions. Dr. Brannock, what survives?

Ilse BrannockThe rotating-spot prediction failed at four-oh-five. The precursor prediction failed on the independent plate. In ten thousand paired shuffles, seven matched both timing and amplitude; ours matched both timings but only one amplitude. The data still prefers schedule-response. It does not prove a mind, and the faster cadence may be a cost of asking.

Dov AchterbergThen stop asking and load the ferries. The experiment changed the thing we feared. And it told every smuggler on the outer rail what hour to move.

Pell RourkeOr exposed that it was already waiting for gaps we happened to give it. The Day Four burst remains the dangerous one. Capping the Day Three dusk peak alone takes my median from one point three to about one point zero. Turning the parasol before dawn takes it to about nine-tenths. What the bounded silence adds I cannot separate from the rest, and I will not pretend to. Together, eight-tenths.

Dov AchterbergMedian. Your upper edge?

Pell RourkeNine-tenths. At the cancel line.

The two numbers stayed between them. Vance looked not at Illuminara but at Ilse.

Teodora VanceIf we stay, what do you ask the Wick to do?

Ilse BrannockNothing beyond what the dangerous burst may do anyway. One bounded silence at dawn, three pulses from our cutter, then no second request. If the flare comes in the window and under the line, we learn whether leaving room changes the load. If not, the manifests are already cut.

Gideon FarrowThe cap costs the guild its best settlement of the quarter, on the Day Three dusk. We will take it once. Not daily, and not without the loss entered beside the science.

Dov AchterbergAnd the notice. The tug at lock six knew seven o'clock because we gave it thirteen hours. No fixed daily blackout, and no posted hour. The Chair chooses inside a ninety-minute band and announces it fifteen minutes ahead. The red channel stays open. Security may cancel without your permission. And the tug is mine to answer for, not the science's.

Nadim OyelaranI can enforce that in hardware. Trade carrier dark; red carrier live; plate independent. Six signatures to change it.

Illuminara had come in with a posted window and was leaving with a hidden one. She wrote Dov's clause into the draft protocol in his own words, and when he read it over her shoulder he changed one verb back.

Teodora VanceThe ferries stay fuelled. Loading starts within one hour if the plate crosses nine-tenths, the flare leaves the window, the red carrier fails, or security calls the silence unsafe. Anyone may take a berth now. We attempt one bounded exchange at dawn. Dov's moving-window amendment and Farrow's cost ledger are part of the motion.

The vote passed seven to four, not nine to two. Dov voted no. His amendment passed eleven to zero.

Afterward the reply was designed in the communications office. Nadim had the forty-metre ice-cutting array. Ilse had her ledger open to the rising edge of the first requested flare.

Nadim OyelaranI can give it a beam. I can't tell you it will see it.

Ilse BrannockThree pulses on the rhythm of its own rise. Then silence for as long as the pulses took. Heard, and your turn.

IlluminaraNo claim about what it means.

Ilse BrannockNo. Only a courtesy we can withdraw.

06 · A Turn at Four-Oh-Five

Calloway Reach, communications office and Rakel Quay · Day 4, 04:05

Under ordinary traffic the dangerous burst had been forecast at one point three of parasol rating. On the evening of Day Three the guild had capped its dusk peak, and Farrow's ledger carried the loss: the best evening of the quarter. Turning the parasol cost a month's thruster propellant and left Rakel Quay outside its full shadow. Rourke's registered range was seven-tenths to nine-tenths. Nine-tenths remained the line.

The Chair chose four-oh-five from the ninety-minute band and announced it fifteen minutes before. The red carrier stayed live. In the communications office Nadim held the beam trigger. On Rakel Quay his sister Kemi and two riggers waited beside the relay-mast breakers, because the model said the exposed masts would take the first side-load.

Kemi OyelaranRakel ready. You owe me two masts if your polite sun sneezes.

Nadim OyelaranPut them on Farrow's ledger.

Gideon FarrowThey are already there.

At four-oh-five Nadim sent three pulses. The trade band remained silent afterward. A medical call crossed the red carrier from nursery six; a child had swallowed a button. The silence did not make the ring helpless.

Four minutes passed.

The independent plate climbed.

Pell RourkePoint six. Point seven-two. Parasol taking thirty-one percent.

A second shoulder rose under the first.

Teodora VanceRead the plate, not the model.

Pell RourkePoint eight-six.

At Rakel, the first mast began to arc. Kemi cut its breaker before the automatic relay understood what was happening. The mast folded across an empty loading rail. The second leaned toward a fuel line.

Kemi OyelaranLosing west two. Clearing the line now.

She drove the quay tug into the mast's lower brace. Metal went down away from the fuel line, taking the tug's manipulator arm with it.

Nadim OyelaranKemi?

Kemi OyelaranStill expensive.

The plate touched eighty-nine hundredths. For twelve seconds its uncertainty band crossed the line, though the central reading did not.

Teodora VanceRourke.

Pell RourkeCentral reading below nine. Structure stable. My recommendation is hold, Chair. Your line says over, not near.

Vance's finger rested on the loading order. She could have called uncertainty a trigger. Nobody would have blamed her.

Teodora VanceHold. Kemi has the quay. Red carrier is live. If the central plate rises one hundredth, load.

It did not. The long shoulder fell through eight-tenths, then seven. The parasol held. Rakel lost two relay masts and one tug arm; no one was hurt.

In the decay, with Nadim's array still silent and the ring keeping the space it had promised, the independent plate drew three small steps.

Ilse BrannockThree. I have nine years and it has never made three.

IlluminaraDon't read it yet. We don't know that it's a reply.

Ilse BrannockNo. We know only that it happened after our three.

They did not repeat the request that night. The next day the council authorized one movable window, with the red channel and security veto intact, and required a fresh vote every seven days. Dov's desk added a standing check of the outer rail to every window, a duty the protocol still carries under his name. Farrow entered the lost settlement, two masts, a tug arm and a month of propellant in the same ledger as the avoided evacuation. Dov signed the safety protocol and wrote beneath his name that he still believed they should leave.

Teodora VanceHe is allowed to be wrong in the record, if he is wrong.

IlluminaraSo are we.

Ilse closed her ledger, opened it again, and wrote on the next clean line in her small upright hand: Four-oh-five. We stopped. It knocked.

ZVEZDA, KI JE GOVORILA SAMO Z IZBRUHI

01 · Sedemdeset ur

Calloway Reach, dvorana sveta obroča · 1. dan, 06:10

Ura na steni dvorane je kazala 70:00:00. Nekdo jo je postavil tja zato, da bi čas izgovorili naglas, pa ga ni nihče. Zunaj dolgega okna se je obroč počasi vrtel pod rdečo zvezdo, veliko kakor kovanec, na njegovi notranji strani je živelo štirinajst tisoč ljudi, v prostoru pa je dišalo po hladnem čaju in svetu, ki ni spal.

Illuminara je tri tedne prej prispela na krovu lednega tenderja; zadruga Rakel jo je najela, da modelira, kako toplota in svetloba obremenjujeta rezalne pomole. V dvorani je bila, ker so bili njeni modeli edini, s katerimi se še nihče ni prepiral. Stala je zadaj ob vrču z vodo.

Teodora VanceWick je v enajstih dneh sprožil šest nevarnih izbruhov. V devetih letih zapisov je sprožil približno enega na mesec. Enajst dni je dvesto štiriinšestdeset ur; šest izbruhov v tem času pomeni enega na štiriinštirideset ur, tega pa ne morem spraviti med nihanja ozadja. Kopičijo se po naših večernih prometnih konicah. Naslednja naravna poravnava se pričakuje okoli štirih zjutraj četrtega dne. Ob običajnem prometu urad za ščit napoveduje eno celo tri nazivne zmogljivosti našega senčnika. Trajekti potrebujejo šestindvajset ur, da končajo natovarjanje, jaz pa iz življenj na obroču ne bom izrezala dvourne rezerve. Ukaz mora biti izdan do dvainštiridesete ure.

Pell RourkeSenčnik prenese en izbruh. Ne bom obljubil, da prenese tistega.

IlluminaraKaj stane odhod?

Teodora VanceRakel. Vse, kar rudarimo. Obroč, ki odide, s seboj odnese osem mesecev vode, potem pa postane zelo velik kozarec.

Vance je bila stara šestdeset let in širokih ramen, navado pa je imela najprej povedati najslabše število, da ji nihče ne bi mogel očitati prikrivanja. Od okna se je obrnila proti zadnjemu delu prostora.

Teodora VanceNe govorite mi, da govori. Nikakor ne moremo vedeti, ali sploh govori, vi pa od štirinajst tisoč ljudi zahtevate, naj ostanejo pod morebitnim orožjem na podlagi vzorca. Če se jaz motim glede orožja, izgubimo led in leto dni. Če se motite vi, izgubimo obroč.

IlluminaraNe bom vam govorila, da govori. Nisem videla dovolj, da bi to trdila, in prav bi imeli, če mi ne bi verjeli. Potrebujem vaš dnevnik prometa po pristaniški uri, dnevnik izbruhov doktorice Brannock, specifikacije vseh detektorjev in ta prostor do večerne seje.

Teodora VanceSvet zaseda ob osemnajstih. Ob osemnajstih dam evakuacijo na glasovanje.

IlluminaraPotem vam bom pred glasovanjem prinesla nekaj, kar lahko preizkusite.

Vance je pogledala uro in nato njo. Radovednost ji ni omehčala obraza; odgovornost na njem je naredila natančnejšo.

Teodora VanceS čim boste to preizkusili? Imamo devetinšestdeset ur in enainpetdeset minut.

02 · Devet let robnih zapiskov

Observatorij obroča, pisarna Brannockove · 1. dan, 09:30

Ilse Brannock je dnevnik izbruhov vodila v knjigi in na omrežju, ker knjige ni mogel urejati nihče, ki mu vsebina ni bila všeč. Devet let Wicka jo je polnilo noč za nočjo, z drobno pokončno pisavo in vprašanji ob robovih. Nekaj jih je bilo dvakrat podčrtanih.

Ilse BrannockVi ste ženska za led s toplotnimi modeli.

IlluminaraDanes sem ženska za led, ki je prebrala vaš dnevnik izbruhov. Zelo čist je. Kdo ga vodi?

IlluminaraVi ne mislite tako.

Ilse je položila dlan na knjigo, kakor bi jo položila na spečo žival.

Ilse BrannockTo sem pokazala dvema človekoma. Eden se je zasmejal, prijazno, kar je bilo še huje. Rekla sem, da Wick postane glasnejši, ko postanemo glasnejši mi. Po vsakem prometnem večeru je naslednji izbruh večji za približno enak delež. Zvezdini izbruhi se ne menijo za našo trgovino. Vedela sem, kako zveni, zato sem o tem nehala govoriti.

IlluminaraKaj pa čas?

Ilse BrannockVedno v vrzeli. Rekla sem ji zgodnje ure, ker smo ji takrat vedno dajali vrzel.

Illuminara je dnevnik prometa položila čez dnevnik izbruhov na stekleni mizi. Ura observatorija in pristaniška ura sta se razlikovali za tri minute. Nihče zapisov ni držal skupaj, ker je borzno omrežje prenašalo zasebne posle.

Eno sled je premaknila za tri minute. Svetle oznake so padle v doline prometa kakor kovanci v mošnjo.

Ilse BrannockŠtiri nič pet. Menjava izmene. Obroč za dvajset minut utihne, medtem ko se ekipe zamenjajo.

IlluminaraVelikost sledi glasnosti pred vrzeljo. Čas sledi sami vrzeli. Če je tukaj namen, najmanj pretirana razlaga ni jeza. Je izmenjava besede: nekaj dvigne glas nad množico in nato čaka, da ga ne prepišemo. Toda enako sled bi še vedno lahko povzročili vrteča se pega, predhodni pojav, ki zatre naš pas, ali naključje.

Ilse BrannockPovejte, kaj želite narediti.

IlluminaraPremakniti vrzel. Štiri nič pet zapolniti z običajnim prometom, odpreti novo vrzel ob sedmih in vsako napoved zapisati, preden se dotaknemo stikal.

IlluminaraKaj ga ne uporablja?

Ilse BrannockStara bolometrična plošča. Žična povezava, ločena ura, nič v borznem pasu. Rourke jo je hotel zavreči.

IlluminaraPotem ostane. Preizkus pa predstavite vi. Ne bom si izposodila devetih let vašega poslušanja in temu rekla svoje odkritje.

Ilse je pogledala dvakrat podčrtano vprašanje v svojem dnevniku. Upanje ni dokaz, je pomislila Illuminara. Toda sram lahko leta skriva dokaz, če nihče ne naredi prostora človeku, ki ga nosi.

Illuminara je obrnila strani dnevnika nazaj k najhujšim izbruhom in naprej k napovedi za četrti dan ter se ustavila. Preizkus bi jim povedal, ali zvezda sledi času. Ne bi zmanjšal izbruha, ki je že prihajal.

IlluminaraŠe nekaj, in to je vprašanje o vaših robnih zapiskih. Če velikost sledi glasnosti pred vrzeljo, izbruh četrtega dne ni določen. Prav zdaj mu velikost daje to, kar počnemo tretji dan zvečer. Kaj se zgodi z izbruhom po tihem večeru?

Ilse je obrnila osem strani, ne da bi jih iskala. Najmanjši izbruhi v knjigi so bili vsi tam: noči po prazniku žetve, ko je obroč potemnel in je bil trgovski pas do mraka skoraj prazen.

Ilse BrannockMajhni. Najmanjši v knjigi so. Pripisala sem jih koledarju.

IlluminaraPotem je vzvod večerna konica, ne vrzel. Če lahko svet omeji promet enega večera pred poravnavo četrtega dne, bo senčnik morda dobil nekaj blizu osmih desetin namesto ena cele tri. Pell bo to moral modelirati. Tega ne morem obljubiti. Lahko vam povem, katero številko naj poskusite premakniti.

Ilse BrannockPredstavila bom, če bodo v ovojnici načini, kako se lahko motim.

IlluminaraPostavite jih na prvo mesto.

03 · Argument za beg

Dvorana sveta · 1. dan, 18:00

Vance je sejo začela tako, da je na glas prebrala uro: oseminpetdeset ur in deset minut. Nato je dala besedo Rourku, ki je stal z rokami za hrbtom kakor človek, ki pričuje na sojenju, za katero upa, da ga bo izgubil.

Pell RourkeNevarna poravnava ob zori četrtega dne, običajen promet, ena cela tri nazivne zmogljivosti. Naši dve zahtevani preizkusni vrzeli lahko pred tem prikličeta manjša odziva. Če ju, bo to novo vedenje, ne sedmi in osmi člen starega zaporedja. Lahko okrepi razlago o izmenjavi besede ali pa pomeni, da poskus sam povečuje nevarnost.

Teodora VanceTo je argument za beg in povedala ga bom sama, da nihče ne bo mislil, da ga nisem upoštevala. Evakuacije propadejo, ko se začnejo prepozno. Zvezda, ki se spremeni, ker jo prosimo, ni samodejno varnejša od zvezde, ki se ne.

Gideon Farrow je vstal s klopi ceha. Bil je okrogel, brezhibno oblečen in vso sejo je nekaj štel v glavi.

Gideon FarrowKdo plača, če zbežimo pred vremenskim pojavom? Led je plača mojega ceha in pitna voda obroča. Ne more veljati, da nihče ne sme vprašati, ali je zvezda samo zvezda.

Teodora VanceNihče tega ni prepovedal. Doktorica Brannock?

Ilse je vstala. Roke na govorniškem pultu so bile mirne, Illuminara pa jo je tri vrste zadaj videla najti zapiske, za katere je nameravala, da jih ne bo potrebovala.

Teodora VanceKoliko naključja?

Sedem parov je ujelo izbruhe v obeh časovnih oknih in obeh pasovih amplitude. Sedem od deset tisoč ni nič. Prav tako ni argument, ki bi ga zavrgla.

Dov AchterbergIzračun, zgrajen iz istega dnevnika, ki je nakazal vprašanje. In vaša okna so široka petdeset minut.

Ilse BrannockDa. Zato so napovedi pege in predhodnega pojava zapečatene poleg naših. Če pega sproži ob stari uri, izgubimo. Če borzni pas odpove, medtem ko je neodvisna plošča tiha, izgubimo. Če en zahtevani rezultat zgreši, napišemo zgrešeno, preden kar koli razlagamo.

IlluminaraJutri ob štiri nič pet zapolnimo običajno vrzel z običajnim prometom. Ob sedmih za dvaindvajset minut ustavimo borzno omrežje. Neodvisna plošča ostane vključena. Po naslednji večerni konici ponovimo s krajšo vrzeljo. Obstaja še drugi vzvod, na katerega kaže sam dnevnik. Velikost sledi glasnosti pred vrzeljo, zato izbruhu četrtega dne velikost daje večer tretjega dne. Če ceh omeji tisto eno konico ob mraku, bi morala Pellova mediana pasti precej pod nazivno zmogljivost senčnika. Tudi to je napoved in tudi ta lahko spodleti. Svet napiše pogoje za prekinitev.

Gideon FarrowKaj premor stane moje trgovce? In kaj jih stane vaša omejitev?

IlluminaraPovejte prostoru, kaj morajo ohraniti.

Dov AchterbergPa tudi ne bi smeli. Načrtovana tišina je načrtovana ranljivost. Zdravniški klici, opozorila pred trki, tihotapci, ki vedo, kdaj nihče ne gleda. Če predlagano zdravilo zahteva, da štirinajst tisoč ljudi po urniku ogluši, imam raje trajekte.

Nadim OyelaranOzek rdeči kanal, strojno omejen na alarme in zdravstvene pogovore. Plošča ga ne bo videla. Za trajno okno lahko predsednica izbere čas znotraj devetdesetminutnega pasu in ga napove petnajst minut prej.

Teodora VanceZapisano. Moja meja za prekinitev: vsak zahtevani izbruh nad devetimi desetinami, vsak izbruh zunaj obeh registriranih oken, vsaka odpoved neodvisne plošče ali vsaka odpoved rdečega kanala. Trajekti bodo nocoj napolnjeni z gorivom in seznami potnikov sestavljeni. Sprožilec začne natovarjanje v eni uri; dokončanje še vedno traja šestindvajset. Tega stavka pozneje nihče ne popravlja.

04 · Vrzel se premakne

Komunikacijski urad, borzno omrežje · 2. dan, 06:52

Ob štiri nič pet so staro vrzel zapolnili in Wick ni rekel ničesar. Borzni pas je ostal čist; prav tako neodvisna bolometrična plošča. Ilse je bila budna od prejšnjega jutra in je sedela zelo vzravnano na stolu, ki ga ni izbrala.

Nadim OyelaranZapečatena ovojnica je v zapisniku sveta. Vrtenje je napovedalo štiri nič pet, kar se ni zgodilo. Predhodni pojav je napovedal, da bo tam borzni pas odpovedal, plošča pa bo ostala tiha, kar se ni zgodilo. Izmenjava besede napoveduje sedmo uro, znotraj petindvajsetih minut, med polovico in sedmimi desetinami nazivne zmogljivosti.

Premor je bil prejšnji večer objavljen v zapisniku sveta, da bi ga pričakoval vsak urad. Ob sedmih je borzno omrežje utihnilo. Kuhinje so delovale, trajekti so ostali napolnjeni z gorivom, rdeči kanal za nujne primere pa je šepetal z dvema zdravstvenima klicema in enim opozorilom pred trkom. Trgovsko nadstropje se je ustavilo za dvaindvajset minut, ko se je štirinajst tisoč ljudi strinjalo, da pustijo prostor.

Žično povezana plošča je risala ravno črto, nato še eno ravno črto, nato pa oster poteg ob sedmih in dveh minutah. Omrežni nadzornik mu je sledil delček sekunde pozneje. Dolga rama pojemanja je bila znamenje, ki ga je Ilse devet let risala v svoj dnevnik.

Ilse BrannockOseminpetdeset stotink na plošči.

Nadim OyelaranZnotraj časa in amplitude. Rdeči kanal ni nikoli izpadel.

Nihče ni vzkliknil. Illuminara je prijela Ilse za komolec šele potem, ko je starejša ženska segla k njej.

Ilse BrannockEna.

IlluminaraEna.

Ob sedmih in šest minut je tovorni vlačilec na zunanji tirnici ugasnil svoj oddajnik in začel drseti proti carinski zapornici. Dovova varnostna služba ga je opazila samo zato, ker je alarm zapornice potoval po rdečem kanalu, služba pa je imela štiri minute, da zapornico zapečati, preden jo je dosegla posadka vlačilca.

Dov AchterbergZapornica šest je zapečatena. Vlačilec se je vrnil na privez. Našo uro so poznali, ker smo jo objavili.

To je povedal prostoru, ne Illuminari, in ni rekel saj sem vam povedal. Ime vlačilca je šlo v zapisnik poleg minut.

Druga zahtevana vrzel je prišla istega dne ob dvaindvajsetih trideset, po manjši večerni konici od prejšnjega večera: zastoj trajektov, ki ga ceh ni načrtoval. Enajst minut pred premorom se je na borznem nadzorniku pokazal šibek dvig. Dov, ki je gledal prenos sveta, ga je razglasil za predhodni pojav. Žično povezana plošča je ostala ravna.

Ob dvaindvajsetih šestintrideset je Wick izbruhnil. Registrirani pas amplitude se je končal pri štiridesetih stotinkah. Plošča se je dvignila na enainštirideset.

Dov AchterbergZunaj ovojnice.

Ilse BrannockZa eno stotinko. Zgrešeno je.

Nadim OyelaranZgodnji dvig je bil naš nosilec, ki je uhajal v borzni nadzornik. Na plošči ga ni. To zavrne trditev o predhodnem pojavu, amplitude pa ne spravi nazaj v ovojnico.

Pell RourkeDva zahtevana odziva v šestnajstih urah sta tudi hitrejša od že tako zgoščene štiriinštirideseturne pogostosti, s katero smo začeli. Če ju povzročamo mi, je to pomembnejše od tega, ali smo sonce naučili manir.

Illuminara je preučila obe sledi in svoje napovedi ni reševala. Ob drugi sledi je Ilse zapisala večerno konico, ob prvi pa prejšnji večer. Številki je položila drugo ob drugo in ju pustila brez komentarja.

Ilse BrannockOseminpetdeset stotink po glasnem večeru. Enainštirideset po tihem.

Pell RourkeEn par.

Ilse BrannockEn par. Šel je v pravo smer. Ni zakon in kot zakon ga ne bom zapisala.

IlluminaraZapišite zadetek časa, zgrešeno amplitudo, zavrnjenega tekmeca s predhodnim pojavom, hitrejšo pogostost in par večerov. Nato ne odpirajte več vrzeli, dokler svet ne odloči, kaj hitrejša pogostost pomeni.

Ilse BrannockŽeleli ste drugo noč.

IlluminaraŽelela sem odgovor, ki bi nam lahko rekel ne. Ta nam je.

05 · Štirideset ur

Dvorana sveta · 2. dan, 23:10

Ob enainštirideseti uri je bila dvorana polna, na steni je ostalo devetindvajset ur, do časa, ko bi moral biti izdan ukaz, pa ena. Pod uro so stale štiri neomiljene vrstice: TIŠINA V STARI VRZELI; PRVA ZAHTEVA ZADETA; DRUGA ZAHTEVA ZADET ČAS / ZGREŠENA AMPLITUDA; ZAHTEVANA POGOSTOST HITREJŠA OD OZADJA.

Teodora VanceNihče v tem prostoru tega ne sme imenovati dve čisti napovedi. Doktorica Brannock, kaj ostane?

Ilse BrannockNapoved vrteče se pege je ob štiri nič pet spodletela. Napoved predhodnega pojava je spodletela na neodvisni plošči. Pri deset tisoč premešanih parih se jih je sedem ujemalo v času in amplitudi; naša sta se ujemala v obeh časih, toda le v eni amplitudi. Podatki še vedno dajejo prednost odzivu na urnik. Ne dokazujejo uma, hitrejša pogostost pa je lahko cena spraševanja.

Dov AchterbergPotem nehajte spraševati in natovorite trajekte. Poskus je spremenil stvar, ki smo se je bali. Vsakemu tihotapcu na zunanji tirnici je tudi povedal, ob kateri uri naj se premakne.

Pell RourkeAli pa je razkril, da je že čakala na vrzeli, ki smo ji jih po naključju dajali. Izbruh četrtega dne ostaja nevaren. Sama omejitev konice ob mraku tretjega dne zniža mojo mediano z ene cele tri na približno ena celo nič. Obrat senčnika pred zoro jo zniža na približno devet desetin. Kar doda omejena tišina, ne morem ločiti od preostalega in ne bom se pretvarjal, da lahko. Skupaj: osem desetin.

Dov AchterbergMediana. Vaš zgornji rob?

Pell RourkeDevet desetin. Na meji za prekinitev.

Številki sta ostali med njima. Vance ni pogledala Illuminare, temveč Ilse.

Teodora VanceČe ostanemo, kaj prosite Wick, naj naredi?

Ilse BrannockNičesar več od tega, kar bi nevarni izbruh morda naredil že tako. Ena omejena tišina ob zori, trije impulzi našega rezalnika, nato nobene druge zahteve. Če izbruh pride v oknu in pod mejo, izvemo, ali puščanje prostora spremeni obremenitev. Če ne, so seznami potnikov že sestavljeni.

Gideon FarrowOmejitev ceh stane najboljšo poravnavo poslov v četrtletju, ob mraku tretjega dne. Enkrat jo bomo sprejeli. Ne vsak dan in ne brez izgube, zapisane poleg znanosti.

Dov AchterbergIn napoved. Vlačilec pri zapornici šest je vedel za sedmo uro, ker smo mu dali trinajst ur časa. Nobenega stalnega dnevnega izklopa in nobene objavljene ure. Predsednica izbere znotraj devetdesetminutnega pasu in jo napove petnajst minut prej. Rdeči kanal ostane odprt. Varnost lahko prekliče brez vašega dovoljenja. In za vlačilec odgovarjam jaz, ne znanost.

Nadim OyelaranTo lahko strojno uveljavim. Trgovski nosilec temen; rdeči nosilec živ; plošča neodvisna. Za spremembo je potrebnih šest podpisov.

Illuminara je vstopila z objavljenim oknom in odhajala s skritim. Dovovo določilo je v osnutek protokola zapisala z njegovimi besedami, on pa je med branjem čez njeno ramo en glagol spremenil nazaj.

Teodora VanceTrajekti ostanejo napolnjeni z gorivom. Natovarjanje se začne v eni uri, če plošča preseže devet desetin, če izbruh zapusti okno, če rdeči nosilec odpove ali če varnost razglasi tišino za nevarno. Kdor želi, lahko že zdaj zasede privez. Ob zori poskusimo eno omejeno izmenjavo. Dovov amandma o premičnem oknu in Farrowov dnevnik stroškov sta del predloga.

Glasovanje se je končalo s sedmimi glasovi proti štirim, ne z devetimi proti dvema. Dov je glasoval proti. Njegov amandma je bil sprejet z enajst proti nič.

Nato so v komunikacijskem uradu zasnovali odgovor. Nadim je imel štiridesetmetrsko polje za rezanje ledu. Ilse je imela dnevnik odprt pri naraščajočem robu prvega zahtevanega izbruha.

Nadim OyelaranLahko mu pošljem žarek. Ne morem vam povedati, da ga bo videlo.

Ilse BrannockTrije impulzi v ritmu njegovega naraščanja. Nato tišina, dolga toliko, kot so trajali impulzi. Slišano, zdaj si na vrsti.

IlluminaraBrez trditve o tem, kaj pomeni.

Ilse BrannockBrez. Samo vljudnost, ki jo lahko umaknemo.

06 · Beseda ob štiri nič pet

Calloway Reach, komunikacijski urad in pomol Rakel · 4. dan, 04:05

Ob običajnem prometu je bil nevarni izbruh napovedan pri eni celi tri nazivne zmogljivosti senčnika. Tretji dan zvečer je ceh omejil konico ob mraku, Farrowov dnevnik pa je nosil izgubo: najboljši večer četrtletja. Obračanje senčnika je stalo mesečno zalogo pogonskega goriva, pomol Rakel pa je ostal zunaj njegove polne sence. Rourkov registrirani razpon je bil od sedmih do devetih desetin. Devet desetin je ostalo meja.

Predsednica je iz devetdesetminutnega pasu izbrala štiri nič pet in čas napovedala petnajst minut prej. Rdeči nosilec je ostal živ. V komunikacijskem uradu je Nadim držal sprožilec žarka. Na pomolu Rakel so njegova sestra Kemi in dva monterja čakali ob odklopnikih relejnih jamborov, ker je model napovedal, da bodo izpostavljeni jambori prevzeli prvo stransko obremenitev.

Kemi OyelaranRakel pripravljen. Če vaše vljudno sonce kihne, mi dolgujete dva jambora.

Nadim OyelaranDaj ju v Farrowov dnevnik.

Gideon FarrowŽe sta v njem.

Ob štiri nič pet je Nadim poslal tri impulze. Trgovski pas je potem ostal tih. Po rdečem nosilcu je prišel zdravstveni klic iz jasli šest; otrok je pogoltnil gumb. Tišina obroča ni naredila nemočnega.

Minile so štiri minute.

Neodvisna plošča se je začela dvigati.

Pell RourkeNič cela šest. Nič cela dvainsedemdeset. Senčnik prevzema enaintrideset odstotkov.

Pod prvim se je dvignila druga rama.

Teodora VanceBerite ploščo, ne modela.

Pell RourkeNič cela šestinosemdeset.

Na Rakelu je prvi jambor začel obločno prebijati. Kemi je njegov odklopnik izključila, preden je samodejni rele razumel, kaj se dogaja. Jambor se je zložil čez prazno nakladalno tirnico. Drugi se je nagnil proti cevi za gorivo.

Kemi OyelaranIzgubljamo zahodni dve. Zdaj čistim cev.

Pomolski vlačilec je zapeljala v spodnjo oporo jambora. Kovina je padla stran od cevi za gorivo in s seboj odnesla upravljalno roko vlačilca.

Nadim OyelaranKemi?

Kemi OyelaranŠe vedno drago.

Plošča se je dotaknila devetinosemdesetih stotink. Dvanajst sekund je njen pas negotovosti sekal mejo, čeprav je osrednji odčitek ni.

Teodora VanceRourke.

Pell RourkeOsrednji odčitek pod devetimi desetinami. Struktura stabilna. Priporočam, da vztrajamo, predsednica. Vaša meja pravi nad, ne blizu.

Vance je držala prst na ukazu za natovarjanje. Negotovost bi lahko razglasila za sprožilec. Nihče ji ne bi očital.

Teodora VanceVztrajamo. Kemi obvladuje pomol. Rdeči nosilec je živ. Če se osrednja plošča dvigne za eno stotinko, natovarjamo.

Ni se. Dolga rama je padla skozi osem desetin, nato sedem. Senčnik je zdržal. Rakel je izgubil dva relejna jambora in eno roko vlačilca; poškodovan ni bil nihče.

Med pojemanjem, ko je Nadimovo polje še molčalo in je obroč držal prostor, ki ga je obljubil, je neodvisna plošča narisala tri majhne stopnice.

Ilse BrannockTri. Imam devet let in nikoli ni naredilo treh.

IlluminaraNe berite jih še. Ne vemo, ali je to odgovor.

Ilse BrannockNe. Vemo le, da se je zgodilo po naših treh.

Tisto noč zahteve niso ponovili. Naslednji dan je svet odobril eno premično okno z ohranjenima rdečim kanalom in varnostnim vetom ter zahteval novo glasovanje vsakih sedem dni. Dovov urad je vsakemu oknu dodal stalni pregled zunanje tirnice, dolžnost, ki jo protokol še vedno nosi pod njegovim imenom. Farrow je izgubljeno poravnavo, dva jambora, roko vlačilca in mesečno zalogo goriva vpisal v isti dnevnik kot preprečeno evakuacijo. Dov je podpisal varnostni protokol in pod svojim imenom zapisal, da še vedno verjame, da bi morali oditi.

Teodora VanceV zapisu se sme motiti, če se moti.

IlluminaraTudi mi se smemo.

Ilse je zaprla dnevnik, ga znova odprla in v svoji drobni pokončni pisavi na naslednjo prazno vrstico zapisala: Štiri nič pet. Ustavili smo se. Potrkalo je.

THE FIRE THAT KNEW HOW TO BURN

An eighty-one-year-old woman has lit forty-one small fires on a hill the fire service wants emptied, and the only way to prove she is right is to find the one place her map is wrong.

01 · Burns by the Wall

Sorrel Gate, upper terraces · 12:40

Smoke stood on the western ridge, six kilometres off and leaning toward them. The district had given Sorrel Gate until three o'clock. Illuminara had spent the morning walking the upper terraces with a tablet of creek gauges, which was what the regional water office had sent her to do, and she had stopped doing it at the first black patch.

There were forty-one of them now. Each was the size of a tablecloth. Each was still warm when she held her palm an inch above it. None lay in open grass. Every one lay on the sheltered side of a drystone wall or the lip of a terrace, and not one had crossed the stone.

Someone is counting the wind, she thought. Someone is lighting only where the wind has been refused.

Taavi Brandt came up the track with a drip torch hanging unlit from his belt and a young crew lead named Joss Marren a pace behind. He was fifty-odd and broad, with the stillness of a man who had learned to spend his words last.

Taavi BrandtSomebody has been lighting my hill since six this morning. Eleven fires I can account for. I'd put the rest on the same hand.

IlluminaraForty-one. I've walked them all.

Taavi BrandtThen you've walked forty-one places where a fire could have got away from a person. Constable Hale is at the church with an order for Ivet Corrandon. She's eighty-one, she won't open her door to my crews, and at dark I carry her down that road myself. I would sooner she walked.

IlluminaraLook at where they are, Chief. Not at who.

He looked, because he was fair and because she had said it quietly. He looked at the nearest patch and the wall above it, and for the length of a breath he said nothing.

Taavi BrandtCalder Fold. Nine years ago. I lit a backburn, lawful and signed, in a wind that behaved for four hours. In the fifth it veered and the fire took the track and then a barn, and there was a man asleep in the barn. Aldous Penn. Careful fires are the ones that kill people. The careless ones don't last long enough.

IlluminaraThen I won't argue that she's careful. I'll ask whether she's right, and look for an instrument that can answer without either of us having to believe anything. Let me speak to her first.

Taavi BrandtUntil two. At two the buses load, and she's on one or she's on my shoulder.

02 · What the Hill Was For

Corrandon cottage, kitchen · 13:15

The door was not locked. Illuminara knocked anyway, and a voice told her through the wood that it never was, that people simply believed it was, and that she could come in if she had the sense to wipe her boots.

Ivet Corrandon sat at the table with ash to the elbows, a match tin at her right hand and a blackthorn stick against her chair. Across her left palm ran a blister the width of a finger. She had the face of someone who had been right for a long time without anyone's help.

Ivet CorrandonYou're the water girl. They said a water girl was on my walls with a machine.

IlluminaraI'm a water-modeller. The machine is a tablet and mostly it counts creeks. May I sit?

Ivet CorrandonIf you've come to take me to the bus you can sit on the floor.

IlluminaraI've no authority to take you anywhere. I came to ask about the wall at the top of Pellam's field.

The old woman looked at her for some time. Illuminara took the clean cloth from the dresser while she waited and asked, with her eyes, about the hand. A question can wait and a blister cannot. Ivet let her do it, watching with open suspicion and then, slowly, with less.

Ivet CorrandonIn nineteen eighty-four a forestry man stood in this kitchen and told my Edrin the hill must not be burned, not by anyone, not ever, and he took the paper that said we could. Edrin was fined. He didn't speak for a week. Forty years we've lived under a hill with nothing to do but grow.

IlluminaraAnd you went on burning.

Ivet CorrandonSmall. At the end of the wet, on the lee of the walls. Edrin called it combing. A fire that comes over a ridge is hungry, and it eats everything between itself and the next thing to eat. Comb the lee of a wall black and the headfire reaches the stone, looks over, and finds nothing for its mouth. A wall with no black behind it is only a stack of stones.

IlluminaraThen why not tell the chief?

Ivet CorrandonHe lit a hill once and a man died. I read it in the paper. He'll hear old woman, and he'll hear liability, and he will not hear wall.

She said it without cruelty, as she might have given the weight of a loaf. Illuminara had been wrong about nothing in this kitchen so far, and she had the feeling that would not last.

Ivet CorrandonAnd you. Your machine has never smelled a slope at four o'clock. It's never stood where the air changes its mind.

IlluminaraNo, it hasn't. So tell me where your map is wrong. I would rather find that here than on the ridge.

Ivet CorrandonNowhere.

The silence went on long enough for the kettle to tick. Ivet looked at the dressed hand, and at the stick, and at the window.

Ivet CorrandonThe north. The gully above the Marrick cottages. I ran out of knee. Edrin never combed the gully. He said it burns itself. Then he never said another word about it, and I never asked.

Something turned over in Illuminara, quietly, like a key in a lock she had been leaning on for three weeks. The gully was the old stone leat, the flood channel she had modelled for the water office. Every storm she had run went down that cut like thread into a needle. Water finds it. So does anything else that wants to go downhill.

IlluminaraMrs Corrandon, would you tell me the order you burn in? Not the reasons. The order. I'll carry it to the chief as something he can test, with his own torch, on his own say.

Ivet CorrandonAnd if his test says I'm a fool?

IlluminaraThen a fool's mistake is corrected in thirty metres, instead of a village's in three hundred. Either way the hill is the winner.

03 · A Test He Could Stop

Sorrel Gate school, command post · 14:05

Two buses idled in the car park with their doors open. Brandt stood over a trestle table with the district map pinned under four stones, and he did not look up until she had laid her tablet on top of his county. Over his shoulder, Joss Marren was loading a hose reel and trying not to listen.

IlluminaraShe isn't lighting fires. She's combing the lee of every wall so a headfire has nothing to eat behind the stone. It's a firebreak drawn in fire. Forty years old, and the state forbade it for all of them.

Taavi BrandtThat's what she says.

IlluminaraIt's what the walls say. I read them as load paths, and a load path is an interpretation, and she could be right by accident. So I'm not asking you to believe her. I'm asking for one segment. Thirty metres of the east wall, your crew, your torch, your hose behind it. If the burn does not die at the lee by itself, you put it out and we've lost twenty minutes.

Taavi BrandtAnd if it dies by itself, I've learned about one wall. The headfire isn't one wall.

IlluminaraNo. But it's a way of turning a coincidence into a measurement. And I'd ask you to hold the second thing against it as well, because I think she's right about the walls and I'm afraid of the place she hasn't burned.

He took a long time. A bus driver coughed. Outside, a woman was counting children from the school into the first coach, name by name, getting each name right.

Taavi BrandtThen these are mine. The buses go at three, all of them, nobody comes off. Anyone not on a bus is crew or on a tanker. The wind goes southwest at about twenty to six, and if the ridge gauge shows a gust past thirty-five, or one ember lands across a wall, I put every flame out and I don't explain myself to you. And the woman stays where I can see her. Not in cuffs. At my shoulder.

IlluminaraShe'll want that. She'll want to be told what she's looking at.

Taavi BrandtHale takes her statement afterwards. She isn't pardoned. If this goes wrong at Calder's rate, I'll want it said that I heard her and chose it, not that she tricked me.

Ivet had arrived at the car park door without being noticed, which at eighty-one and with a stick took talent. She stood in the frame and heard the last of it.

Ivet CorrandonI never asked to be pardoned, Chief.

Taavi BrandtNo. I'm told you never asked anyone for anything. That's most of what's wrong with this.

04 · The Gully

East wall, then the gully head · 16:05

Joss Marren lit thirty metres of the lee at ten past four, with Brandt crouched at his elbow and Ivet in a borrowed folding chair on the track above, her stick across her knees like a sword she had decided not to draw. The flame crept three paces along the grass. It lay down against the stone and went out.

Nobody said anything. A second pass, a little further along: the same. Joss looked at his chief. Brandt put two fingers into the black and held them there.

Taavi BrandtCold.

Ivet CorrandonOf course it's cold. It had nothing to ask for.

Then the smoke from the last small patch did something that Illuminara had been waiting for and did not enjoy being right about. It did not lift. It slid sideways along the ground, thin and grey, leaning north, and went into the mouth of the gully above the Marrick cottages the way water goes into a drain.

IlluminaraChief, look at the smoke. That's my creek. The gully is the old leat, and it is the same shape for air that it is for water. When the wind goes southwest at twenty to six, the headfire won't come at the village over the walls she's combed. It'll come to the one place that has no black behind it, and the leat will take it straight down the cut and out over the top terrace.

Taavi BrandtInto the school and the Marrick cottages.

IlluminaraInto both. And it won't stop at the wall, because no one has burned anything behind that wall for forty years.

Ivet CorrandonEdrin said it burns itself.

IlluminaraWhen did he say it?

Ivet CorrandonThe year after the goats went. Hennie Marrick kept sixty goats on that cut and they ate everything to the clay. Edrin said what he saw. He didn't say the goats had been doing the burning for us.

It was the first time Illuminara had seen the old woman look surprised, and she did not look away from it, out of courtesy. Forty years of a rule that had been right on the day it was spoken.

Taavi BrandtI can't backburn it dry. Not with a headfire two hours out. Dry fuel in a cut that draws like that, I'd be lighting my own chimney.

IlluminaraThen don't burn it dry. The leat has a sluice at the head, and the creek is still running. Forty litres a second for the wet band, down the floor of the cut and over both banks, and a margin either side that your crew combs slow and downhill, Mrs Corrandon's way. A wet strip, a black strip, a wall. The fire has a river on one side and a stone on the other and nowhere to go but out.

Taavi BrandtDownhill. Not up. You said up in your notes.

IlluminaraI did.

Taavi BrandtUp and you're feeding it a ramp. Thirty years I've never lit upslope. Down, a flame has to work for every metre.

IlluminaraDown. Thank you. Then the sluice opens first, and the first torch can't light until the wet front has passed the third terrace. Eleven minutes a hundred metres. If it opens at ten past five, you light at twenty to.

The wheel at the sluice head had not turned since before Illuminara had been in the district. It took Joss and two of Brandt's volunteers and a length of scaffold pipe for a lever, and she stood by with her watch and counted them through it aloud, as one counts a woman in labour. At ten past five the stone throat filled and the cut began to talk.

05 · The Wind Comes Round

Ridge above the gully · 17:41

The wind turned a minute early.

It came off the west like a door opening in a long house, and the smoke that had leaned north for three hours stood up, thought about it, and leaned the other way. The ridge gauge on Brandt's radio read twenty-nine, then thirty-three. His crews were already in their lines: black behind every wall, a wet band shining down the bottom of the cut, a combed margin either side with the last embers of Joss's slow torch still ticking in it.

Taavi BrandtThirty-four on the gauge. One more and it's my line, and I stop everything. Nobody lights anything else. Everybody who's holding, hold.

The headfire arrived at six minutes to six. It did not come as a wave. It came as a noise, then as a colour on the underside of the smoke, then as a line of brightness across the whole west face of the hill with embers going over it like thrown seed. It reached the first wall. It looked over. Illuminara watched it do exactly what an old woman had said it would do, and find nothing for its mouth.

In the gully it was worse and better. The fire went down into the cut because the cut drew it, and met the wet band, and the wet band cooled it to a crawl; it tried both banks and found them combed and black. For forty minutes it hissed and leaned and spat at the stone. Then it ran out of road.

Not everything held. The two Marrick cottages at the north end of the cut lay beyond the strip, because there had been neither time nor water nor crew to carry the break that far, and a gust took an ember across the last wall at six-ten. Joss started toward the tanker.

Taavi BrandtNo. They're empty. Let them go.

Joss MarrenChief, they're Hennie's—

Taavi BrandtThey're stone and slates. Hennie's in the school hall with his dog. If I send one lad up that track and the wind veers again, I've done Calder in a new place. Let them go, Joss.

They went up like paper lanterns, one and then the other, and the whole crew watched them in a silence that Illuminara did not interrupt. Below them the village lay dark and standing. Three hundred roofs. A school with its windows reflecting something that was no longer a threat.

06 · What Remained

Corrandon cottage, kitchen · 21:40

Constable Hale took the statement at the kitchen table with her hat on her knee and was careful to write only what she was told. Ivet gave it with her bandaged hand flat on the wood. When it was done Hale put away her pen and said nothing about permits, because there was a chief in the doorway and it was his to say.

Taavi BrandtThe Marrick cottages are ash. The test burn was lit without a licence, on my say, against the district's written order. I'll answer for both. I'll answer, too, for the look I gave an old woman at midday.

Ivet CorrandonYou gave me a perfectly good look. I'd have given it to you.

Taavi BrandtMy report starts with your map and ends with my abort line. The review can read it in that order.

Ivet CorrandonThey'll fine me.

Taavi BrandtThey may. I'll stand beside you at the hearing and say what I saw on that wall. That isn't a pardon. I can't give you one.

Ivet CorrandonI don't want one. I want it taught.

Brandt turned his hat once in his hands. It was the nearest thing to hesitation the night had left him.

Taavi BrandtThen you'll teach my crews. Mine first, in the dry month, before any licence is argued over. The regional office can quarrel about the paper with a hillside that's still standing.

Ivet said nothing. Edrin's map lay open under the lamp, drawn forty years ago in pencil on the back of a seed catalogue: every wall of Sorrel Gate, each lee shaded. Illuminara drew one more line on it at the north, a thin blue cut with an arrow, and wrote beside it, in her small precise hand, leat and wet band, comb downhill. She turned the paper toward the old woman.

IlluminaraWould you sign it with his name as well? It's the part he never had time to finish.

Ivet took the pencil in her bandaged hand, and wrote, slowly and without once pressing too hard, Edrin Corrandon, and under it, and Ivet.
