The Air the Second-Born Held

On the refinery moon Calder, eight hundred engineered workers with no standing have set the air plants to a slow decline, and Illuminara must find a guarantee strong enough that nobody has to hold a breath hostage again, and a standing no council can vote away.

01 · The Gate Below Nine

Lower Level Nine, Ring Gate · Day one, 06:10

Wren Odira read the numbers off the slate before the lift had finished opening.

Wren OdiraPlant Two is at eighty-two percent of rating and losing two points a day. Oxygen from the tanks covers the gap, but only down to seventy-four. Under that there is not enough reserve to repressurize a deck that takes a breach.

IlluminaraAnd what the tanks cannot cover?

Wren OdiraThe tanks make oxygen. They do not scrub. Level Four read four thousand parts per million of carbon dioxide at midnight. The norm is fifteen hundred.

IlluminaraWho lives on Four?

Wren OdiraThe clinic. The nursery. The old. It is the dead end of the ring, so it fills first.

IlluminaraAnd Plant One?

Wren OdiraForty-one percent of the colony's air, and the engineers say it cannot be pushed past forty-nine. Plant Two is the rest, and it feeds the lower ring. Kesh Aurelian sequences Plant Two. He said day five, and at two points a day, day five is the line.

The corridor beyond the gate was low and warm and smelled of hot metal and boiled grain. Illuminara stood in it and let AC do what it did. It did not read minds. It made the lines of force in a place visible to her, the way a map makes slope visible, and she saw how the people in the corridor leaned. Every body leaned toward the gate. It was not the lean of hostility. It was the posture of people who had been told, all their lives, to wait.

That is a reading, and a reading is a guess about someone else's mouth. Test it before you rest on it. She had been a court interpreter at twenty-four. She had learned that the first meaning always arrives sounding like certainty.

A woman in a grey scrubber-hall coat came out of the crowd and did not offer her hand.

Marit VossMarit Voss. I run the day shift on Two. Kesh said you would ask to see him first.

IlluminaraI would like to start with whoever has to breathe the answer.

Marit VossThat is the wrong answer for a diplomat and I may keep you for it. There are eight hundred of us on this plant. We have run it since before the first of us was born, legally speaking. Come to the hall tonight. They will ask you things. If you answer like a politician nobody opens that door twice.

02 · What the Hall Asked

Scrubber Hall, Plant Two · Day one, 20:00

They sat on the maintenance benches among the great grey cylinders, three hundred of them, the rest listening on the relay. The elder, Osei Tamm, had a voice like a worn gasket and did not stand to speak.

Osei TammNinth Year, the council gave us a charter. Recognition, they called it. We were counted. We were given ration cards with our own names on them. In nineteen months they repealed it. They did not even need a vote against us. A clerk added a column to the census, and we were contract stock again, and the cards stopped working at the canteen. I was forty. I remember the canteen.

IlluminaraAnd since then, every recognition has been used and then taken back.

Osei TammEvery one. Do not say it as if you have learned it from a file. The one thing on this moon they cannot repeal is the air, because it passes through our hands. That is not politics. It is the only fact we have.

Marit VossAsk her what you want to ask her, Teodor. You have been holding it all day.

A young man near the back stood up. His hands were scarred across the knuckles from valve work.

Teodor RaskMy sister is on Level Four. First-born husband, a baby. The ring read forty-one hundred when I came off shift, and I turn the dials that are going down. I am not going to tell you I am proud of it. If this ends with a child on Four in a tent, I did that, and Kesh did that, and I do not know what I am if the price of being a person is that.

Nobody spoke. Marit turned toward the room.

Marit VossI am not a lever. I want that said in front of her. I want my standing. I do not want it bought with somebody's lungs. If the only way we get it is by being the hand on the throat, then they were right about us and I would rather lose.

Osei TammThen you will lose, Marit. Sit down. Both things are true.

Illuminara waited until the room had finished being angry. Then she said what she had, which was less than they wanted.

IlluminaraI do not know yet how to give you a guarantee that cannot be taken back. I know three things. I know I cannot ask you to trust me. I know the air has been your only leverage and your worst burden. And I know that if I find nothing, I will say so plainly, and you will have lost nothing but two days.

Osei TammTwo days. That is an honest sum. Come back when you have something that does not need us to like you.

03 · The Number Behind the Council

Council Chamber, Upper Ring · Day two, 09:15

Speaker Ines Torvald had a clipped, tired manner and did not rise either.

Ines TorvaldWe do not bargain with hostage-takers. If we do, the next group learns the shape of the key. I will hear you out. I will not promise you a concession.

IlluminaraI am not asking you to bargain. I am asking what happens on day five.

Chief Engineer Dov Hallam unrolled a section of the plant schematic across the table. He spoke like a man reading a charge sheet against his own drawings.

Dov HallamDay five is seventy-four. Below that there is no breach margin. I have a cross-feed from the upper tank farm that would let me seal the upper decks' reserve and let the lower ones go short. I drew it at six this morning because it was the thing I could draw.

IlluminaraThen it is a verdict, not a reserve. Fourteen thousand people live below Nine. They did not set the plants. Seal everyone or seal no one.

Pell ArkwrightThe owners will lose four days of throughput if you ration the ore plant to hold the margin for all decks. I am obliged to say so.

IlluminaraSay it and then do it. The cost is real. It is also smaller than a deck that cannot be repressurized.

Dov looked at the cross-feed line, then at her, and rolled it differently, so that the reserve fed all decks to the same floor.

Dov HallamRationing the ore plant by half holds seventy-four for everyone to about day seven. It also frees the power to wake the old scrubber banks on Four through Seven. They need a day and a quarter. The ring will not have its air back before tomorrow noon.

IlluminaraThen someone on Four has a bad night first.

Dov HallamYes. I would rather say it than have you find it.

While they argued the rationing, AC showed her something else. Three lines of dependence ran across the room, from the council, from the owners, from the engineer, and all three ran toward the same place and none of the three looked at it. It was the Registry certificate on the wall behind Dov, off-moon authority, the plant's operating licence.

A hypothesis. Do not say it as a fact.

IlluminaraDov. What does the certificate say about who may run the plant?

Dov HallamRegistry-certified operators. It says nothing about class. The second-born run it under the contract-labour schedule because the owners filed them there thirty years ago and nobody since has put the question to the Registry.

IlluminaraWhat does the Registry do with an operator it has certified?

Dov HallamUnder Article Six, an operator of record is held by the person, not the employer. Name, number, post. The colony can change a worker's census class. It cannot change a record the Registry keeps. Only a finding of cause from the Registry's Review Panel, after a hearing, can remove one.

IlluminaraAnd the article itself? Who can change that?

Dov HallamTwo-thirds of the forty member settlements, in open session, after a hundred and eighty days' notice. Six of them run crews like ours on the same schedule. Nobody here has ever filed a single operator under Six. We have never been in it.

Ines Torvald had stopped looking at her papers.

Ines TorvaldIf the Registry recorded them, I could not repeal it by resolution.

Dov HallamNo. And the insurer would not insure a plant whose operators of record were struck off by a colony vote. Pell could not sell a barrel.

Pell Arkwright said nothing, which was an answer.

Dov HallamOne more thing, since we are being honest. There is an old safety trip on the sequence bus. It forbids sequencing below ninety percent of rating. We bypassed it years ago because it tripped the plant whenever a bearing ran hot.

IlluminaraKeep it. I may want it back.

She turned back to the table, and to the room that had begun, a little, to lean toward the same place.

IlluminaraThen there is a cost to repeal that does not depend on anyone on Calder being kind. I will test whether it is as strong as it sounds. I will test it with the man who has the most reason to doubt it.

04 · The Key and the Throat

Plant Two Control Room · Day three, 14:00

Kesh Aurelian was tall in the way that engineered people sometimes were, designed for a height nobody had asked for, and he stood with his back to the sequencing console as if guarding it from her. Hana Duvall, a nurse from the Level Four clinic, had come up with Illuminara. Illuminara had asked for a first-born resident. Hana had asked for the room.

Kesh AurelianYou have been on my moon for three days and the first thing you do is give the council a way to ration around me.

IlluminaraYes. And I told you within the hour, because if you had found it yourself on day four, you would never have believed anything I said after.

Kesh AurelianYou hedged my five days.

IlluminaraI protected the people who were not part of the argument. That is not the same as protecting them from you. It protects them from the arithmetic.

Kesh took that. His hands, at his sides, did not move.

Kesh AurelianSay what you came to say.

IlluminaraThe eight hundred have never been filed as operators of record. The owners put them on the contract-labour schedule, and the council has been able to do to them what a clerk did in the Ninth Year. Refile them under Article Six. Each of you gets a record the Registry keeps off-moon: your name, not a stock number, your post, your contract in your own hand. You can be moved only by a finding of cause after a hearing. And on the console itself, every shift run by two operators, one second-born and one other, and any sequence change needs both keys.

Kesh AurelianThen I will tell you how they beat it. Tell me where I am wrong. They bring in first-born operators and let ours lapse unused.

IlluminaraA post of record cannot be vacated except by the panel. A cut of more than a tenth of a crew opens a public hearing, a hundred and eighty days.

Kesh AurelianThe census puts us back to contract stock.

IlluminaraThe census is the council's. The record is the Registry's.

Kesh AurelianPell sells the plant to someone who does not care.

IlluminaraThe licence cannot pass without the operators of record. The buyer takes the eight hundred with the plant, or buys nothing.

Kesh AurelianThey change the article.

IlluminaraTwo-thirds of forty settlements, in open session, after a hundred and eighty days. It can be done. It cannot be done quietly. The Ninth Year took nineteen months of quiet. This would take a year of daylight.

Kesh AurelianA year of daylight is still a year. And it is still other people's goodwill.

IlluminaraIt is other people's interest. Six settlements stand on the same article. Goodwill has to be asked for. Interest only has to be noticed.

Kesh looked at the console, not at her. It was the first time he had looked away from her since she came in.

Kesh AurelianSay all of that holds. You still hand me a console with two keys on it. What stops the next Kesh? What stops Jun, or Pell's man, who sits on his key until a bearing fails and says the second-born made him do it? Joint control is a veto in two hands. A hostage needs a hand and a throat. You have given the hands a new throat.

Illuminara did not answer at once. He is not asking to rule. Watch what he is asking for. He did not want the chair. He wanted the thing nobody could take back, and he had just found the flaw in her own design faster than she had.

IlluminaraYou are right. I built that wrong. A veto over the air is still a lever. So take the lever out of the keys. Dov's old trip, the one that forbids sequencing below ninety percent of rating. We put it back, and the Registry seals it, not the council and not you. The keys never decide whether air flows. They decide only when a maintenance window may open, above the floor, with seventy-two hours' notice posted to every deck.

Kesh AurelianAnd below the floor?

IlluminaraNothing lowers it. Break the seal and every deck's alarm sounds and the Registry duty office is paged. The seal holds six hours and then the plant reverts on its own. Any one operator, of any faction, may hold or raise output with no key at all. Only lowering needs two, and lowering below the floor needs a seal nobody can break quietly.

Kesh AurelianJun withholds his key to stop a repair. The bearing fails.

IlluminaraThen Plant Two runs rough until the published window. The floor holds. The cost is a worse week for the engineers, and not a worse week for Level Four.

Kesh AurelianSo the key can only keep the air on.

IlluminaraYes. The worst a withheld key can do is nothing. I do not know whether that is enough for you. It is the only kind of safeguard I can see that does not need a better man than you in the chair after you.

Hana had been standing against the wall. She spoke without moving off it.

Hana DuvallI am not here to be your lever either. I walked up here to tell you that. Level Four read forty-six hundred at midnight. For most of us that is a headache. Anselm Pruitt was seventy-one and had two years of lung left. He could not clear it. His blood turned acid. He died at four this morning. We put the nursery in oxygen tents because we had to do something with our hands, and tents do nothing for carbon dioxide.

Kesh AurelianI read the list.

Hana DuvallThen you know the name.

Kesh AurelianAnselm Pruitt. Yes.

He did not defend it. Illuminara watched him not defend it, and watched the old reflex that said every harm was the fault of those who had made harm necessary rise and die in his throat. He said, quietly, to the room:

Kesh AurelianI drew seventy-four for the oxygen. I knew the ring would climb on carbon dioxide before that. I told myself the clinics could carry it for four days. I wrote the word acceptable in my notes. A man's name sits under that word now.

Hana DuvallThe banks on Four came up at 13:40. The ring is at thirty-nine hundred and falling. That is the first hour in three days I have not had to count breaths. Now you decide what that means.

Kesh did not answer. He stood with his back to the console, and then, slowly, he turned and looked at it.

05 · The Count

Ballot Hall, Lower Level Seven · Day four, 19:30

The second-born voted without Kesh in the room. Marit had insisted, and Osei Tamm had agreed, and Kesh had gone and sat in the plant corridor with his arms folded and looked at nothing. Illuminara stood at the back with Wren and held her tongue while eight hundred people raised their hands under the grey lights.

The elders counted. Marit counted twice.

Osei TammSix hundred and twelve for. A hundred and forty-eight against. Forty abstain.

Teodor RaskI voted against. A record is not a vote. It is a floor under the work, and a name on a shelf off-moon. It is not a door into the house.

IlluminaraYou are right. It is standing of record: your name, your post, a hearing before anyone can move you. It is not a seat on the council and I will not call it one. I would rather say that now than have you find it in a year.

Teodor RaskThen why did you ask us to vote?

IlluminaraBecause I do not get to decide for you what is enough. I get to put an honest thing in front of you, and you get to hold it up and see how it looks.

Marit VossThen the charter is the door, and this is the floor under the door. Let them sign it. If they break it again, there is still a floor under the broken door.

The Registry duty officer, Sabine Okafor-Reyes, appeared on the relay at 20:10 with the refiling: all eight hundred as operators of record under Article Six, the floor interlock sealed under the Registry's own key, the joint-shift rule written into the plant's certificate as a condition of operation, effective on restoration. Beside her signature stood another.

Pell ArkwrightI am obliged to countersign as licence-holder. I find I am relieved to.

Teodor, who read cryptographic signatures for fun, checked the Registry's key against the refiling on his own console. Kesh called the duty officer on a line the council did not control and listened to her say the same words twice.

Kesh AurelianShe says the refiling stands whether the council signs the charter or not.

IlluminaraIt does. I would not give you anything that needed the council's signature to exist.

Kesh AurelianThen I stand down first. Before the charter. Before any reward.

IlluminaraThat is the order I wanted.

The council did not sign that night. Ines Torvald sent word that she would sign at dawn and not before, as if the hour were hers. Illuminara decided that did not matter. The stand-down was Kesh's to make. The signing was the council's to be seen making. Different currencies.

06 · Seventy-Four

Scrubber Hall, Plant Two · Day five, 02:40

Marit and a council engineer named Jun Calloway sat shoulder to shoulder at the sequencing console, each with a key on a chain round the neck, and neither would look at the other. Jun's hands shook. Marit's did not.

Kesh took the open channel and spoke into it the way a man pulls a splinter.

Kesh AurelianThis is Kesh Aurelian. At 02:41 I release the sequencing on Plant Two. I set the plants to decline. A man named Anselm Pruitt is dead of it. I will answer to the Registry's inquiry and to the people of Level Four. The air belongs to all of you now. It always did.

He turned the key in his own lock and set it in Marit's palm. Jun turned his. The console accepted the pair, and the Registry's seal came up green on the bus.

The numbers began to climb. Nobody had to turn a key to raise them. Wren read them out softly, as if loud voices might stall them.

Wren OdiraSeventy-six. Seventy-nine. Eighty-two. The tanks are drawing down.

Marit VossHold it there. Let it rise on its own, not on mine or his.

Jun CallowayI came up here afraid of what you would do with that key.

Marit VossI was afraid of the same about yours.

Jun CallowayI could not lower it now if I tried. Could I?

Dov HallamNeither of you could. Not alone, not together, not without a seal and six hours and every alarm on Calder. That is the point.

Osei Tamm stood at the back of the hall with his arms crossed. He did not look pleased, and Illuminara had not expected him to.

Osei TammA record is not a home. A floor is not a house.

IlluminaraNo. It is where you start from, and nobody can pull it out from under you without paying for it in front of six settlements. That is less than you deserve. It is more than you had on Monday. The ballot on Calder is still the council's to give.

Osei TammHmph. It is a start. I will eat my cap if they keep the second key when the owners change.

IlluminaraThe licence cannot pass without you, the Registry will have the owners to deal with, and you will have Marit to ask.

Hana Duvall came down at 03:30 with a thermos and set it on the console without a word, between two keys.

Hana DuvallFour is at two thousand and falling.

Marit looked at the thermos, and at her, and nodded once. Nothing was forgiven. It was only shared.

By 04:10 Plant Two was at ninety-six percent of rating, the seventy-four line a long way below them, the tanks refilling, and the reserve for every deck on Calder, upper and lower, held to the same floor. The council would sign at dawn. The resentment in the hall would last longer than the signing, and Illuminara did not mind that, because resentment was an honest instrument and it was pointed at something real.

Marit VossI wanted my standing without being the hand on the throat. This is the first thing I have held on this plant that cannot hurt anyone.

She leaned back from the console and breathed in, long, as if testing that it was hers.

Marit VossTwo keys.

IlluminaraTwo keys.

Kesh AurelianSay all of that holds. You still hand me a console with two keys on it. What stops the next Kesh? What stops Jun, or Pell's man, who sits on his key until a bearing fails and says the second-born made him do it? Joint control is a veto in two hands. A hostage needs a hand and a throat. You have given the hands a new throat.

Illuminara did not answer at once. He is not asking to rule. Watch what he is asking for. He did not want the chair. He wanted the thing nobody could take back, and he had just found the flaw in her own design faster than she had.

IlluminaraYou are right. I built that wrong. A veto over the air is still a lever. So take the lever out of the keys. Dov's old trip, the one that forbids sequencing below ninety percent of rating. We put it back, and the Registry seals it, not the council and not you. The keys never decide whether air flows. They decide only when a maintenance window may open, above the floor, with seventy-two hours' notice posted to every deck.

Kesh AurelianAnd below the floor?

IlluminaraNothing reaches it. Not a vote, not a key, not two keys, not an order from me. A window may take one train offline for repair, and only while the plant stays at ninety or above. The one way under is to cut the seal by hand. Then every deck's alarm sounds, the Registry duty office is paged, and the interlock re-arms itself and drives the plant back to rating in six hours, whatever anyone does. And any one operator, of any faction, may hold or raise output with no key at all.

Kesh AurelianSix hours is still six hours.

IlluminaraAt two points a day, six hours is half a point. From ninety, seventy-four is eight days away. Nobody can hold a breath hostage on that clock.

Kesh AurelianJun withholds his key to stop a repair. The bearing fails.

IlluminaraThen Plant Two runs rough until the published window. The floor holds. The cost is a worse week for the engineers, and not a worse week for Level Four.

Kesh AurelianSo the key can only keep the air on.

IlluminaraYes. The worst a withheld key can do is nothing. I do not know whether that is enough for you. It is the only kind of safeguard I can see that does not need a better man than you in the chair after you.

Hana had been standing against the wall. She spoke without moving off it.

Hana DuvallI am not here to be your lever either. I walked up here to tell you that. Level Four read forty-six hundred at midnight, and the dead-end ward past the last vent read nine thousand. For most of us that is a headache. Anselm Pruitt was seventy-one and had two years of lung left. He carried carbon dioxide on a good day. His blood turned acid: seven-twenty-one at two, seven-eighteen at half past three. He died at four this morning. I will not tell you the air alone killed him. Nobody can. It took the last margin he had. We put the nursery in oxygen tents because we had to do something with our hands, and tents do nothing for carbon dioxide.

Kesh AurelianI read the list.

Hana DuvallThen you know the name.

Kesh AurelianAnselm Pruitt. Yes.

He did not defend it. Illuminara watched him not defend it, and watched the old reflex that said every harm was the fault of those who had made harm necessary rise and die in his throat. He said, quietly, to the room:

Kesh AurelianI drew seventy-four for the oxygen. I knew the ring would climb on carbon dioxide before that. I never asked what the dead end would read. I told myself the clinics could carry it for four days. I wrote the word acceptable in my notes. A man's name sits under that word now, beside whatever else was wrong with him.

Hana DuvallThe banks on Four came up at 13:40. The ring is at thirty-nine hundred and falling. That is the first hour in three days I have not had to count breaths. Now you decide what that means.

Kesh did not answer. He stood with his back to the console, and then, slowly, he turned and looked at it.

05 · The Count

Ballot Hall, Lower Level Seven · Day four, 19:30

The second-born voted without Kesh in the room. Marit had insisted, and Osei Tamm had agreed, and Kesh had gone and sat in the plant corridor with his arms folded and looked at nothing. Illuminara stood at the back with Wren and held her tongue while eight hundred people raised their hands under the grey lights.

The elders counted. Marit counted twice.

Osei TammSix hundred and twelve for. A hundred and forty-eight against. Forty abstain.

Teodor RaskI voted against. A record is not a vote. It is a floor under the work, and a name on a shelf off-moon. It is not a door into the house.

IlluminaraYou are right. It is standing of record: your name, your post, a hearing before anyone can move you. It is not a seat on the council and I will not call it one. I would rather say that now than have you find it in a year.

Teodor RaskThen why did you ask us to vote?

IlluminaraBecause I do not get to decide for you what is enough. I get to put an honest thing in front of you, and you get to hold it up and see how it looks.

Marit VossThen the charter is the door, and this is the floor under the door. Let them sign it. If they break it again, there is still a floor under the broken door.

The Registry duty officer, Sabine Okafor-Reyes, appeared on the relay at 20:10 with the refiling: all eight hundred as operators of record under Article Six, the floor interlock sealed under the Registry's own key, the joint-shift rule written into the plant's certificate as a condition of operation, effective on restoration. Beside her signature stood another.

Pell ArkwrightI am obliged to countersign as licence-holder. I find I am relieved to.

Teodor, who read cryptographic signatures for fun, checked the Registry's key against the refiling on his own console. Kesh called the duty officer on a line the council did not control and listened to her say the same words twice.

Kesh AurelianShe says the refiling stands whether the council signs the charter or not.

IlluminaraIt does. I would not give you anything that needed the council's signature to exist.

Kesh AurelianThen I stand down first. Before the charter. Before any reward.

IlluminaraThat is the order I wanted.

The council did not sign that night. Ines Torvald sent word that she would sign at dawn and not before, as if the hour were hers. Illuminara decided that did not matter. The stand-down was Kesh's to make. The signing was the council's to be seen making. Different currencies.

06 · Seventy-Four

Scrubber Hall, Plant Two · Day five, 02:40

Marit and a council engineer named Jun Calloway sat shoulder to shoulder at the sequencing console, each with a key on a chain round the neck, and neither would look at the other. Jun's hands shook. Marit's did not.

Kesh took the open channel and spoke into it the way a man pulls a splinter.

Kesh AurelianThis is Kesh Aurelian. At 02:41 I release the sequencing on Plant Two. I set the plants to decline. A man named Anselm Pruitt is dead, and my setting took the margin he had left. I will answer to the Registry's inquiry and to the people of Level Four. The air belongs to all of you now. It always did.

He turned the key in his own lock and set it in Marit's palm. Jun turned his. The console accepted the pair, and the Registry's seal came up green on the bus.

The numbers began to climb. Nobody had to turn a key to raise them. Wren read them out softly, as if loud voices might stall them.

Wren OdiraSeventy-six. Seventy-nine. Eighty-two. The tanks are drawing down.

Marit VossHold it there. Let it rise on its own, not on mine or his.

Jun CallowayI came up here afraid of what you would do with that key.

Marit VossI was afraid of the same about yours.

Jun CallowayI could not lower it now if I tried. Could I?

Dov HallamNeither of you could. Not alone, not together. The most anyone can do is cut the seal by hand, and then every alarm on Calder sounds and the interlock climbs back on its own in six hours. That is the point.

Osei Tamm stood at the back of the hall with his arms crossed. He did not look pleased, and Illuminara had not expected him to.

Osei TammA record is not a home. A floor is not a house.

IlluminaraNo. It is where you start from, and nobody can pull it out from under you without paying for it in front of six settlements. That is less than you deserve. It is more than you had on Monday. The ballot on Calder is still the council's to give.

Osei TammHmph. It is a start. I will eat my cap if they keep the second key when the owners change.

IlluminaraThe licence cannot pass without you, the Registry will have the owners to deal with, and you will have Marit to ask.

Hana Duvall came down at 03:30 with a thermos and set it on the console without a word, between two keys.

Hana DuvallFour is at two thousand and falling.

Marit looked at the thermos, and at her, and nodded once. Nothing was forgiven. It was only shared.

By 04:10 Plant Two was at ninety-six percent of rating, the seventy-four line a long way below them, the tanks refilling, and the reserve for every deck on Calder, upper and lower, held to the same floor. The council would sign at dawn. The resentment in the hall would last longer than the signing, and Illuminara did not mind that, because resentment was an honest instrument and it was pointed at something real.

Marit VossI wanted my standing without being the hand on the throat. This is the first thing I have held on this plant that cannot hurt anyone.

She leaned back from the console and breathed in, long, as if testing that it was hers.

Marit VossTwo keys.

IlluminaraTwo keys.

The Air the Second-Born Held

On the refinery moon Calder, eight hundred engineered workers with no standing have set the air plants to a slow decline, and Illuminara must find a guarantee strong enough that nobody has to hold a breath hostage again, and a standing no council can vote away.

01 · The Gate Below Nine

Lower Level Nine, Ring Gate · Day one, 06:10

Wren Odira read the numbers off the slate before the lift had finished opening.

Wren OdiraPlant Two is at eighty-two percent of rating and losing two points a day. Oxygen from the tanks covers the gap, but only down to seventy-four. Under that there is not enough reserve to repressurize a deck that takes a breach.

IlluminaraAnd what the tanks cannot cover?

Wren OdiraThe tanks make oxygen. They do not scrub. Level Four read four thousand parts per million of carbon dioxide at midnight. The norm is fifteen hundred.

IlluminaraWho lives on Four?

Wren OdiraThe clinic. The nursery. The old. It is the dead end of the ring, so it fills first, and the clinic's last ward sits past the final vent where the air barely moves.

IlluminaraAnd Plant One?

Wren OdiraForty-one percent of the colony's air, and the engineers say it cannot be pushed past forty-nine. Plant Two is the rest, and it feeds the lower ring. Kesh Aurelian sequences Plant Two. He said day five, and at two points a day, day five is the line.

The corridor beyond the gate was low and warm and smelled of hot metal and boiled grain. Illuminara stood in it and let AC do what it did. It did not read minds. It made the lines of force in a place visible to her, the way a map makes slope visible, and she saw how the people in the corridor leaned. Every body leaned toward the gate. It was not the lean of hostility. It was the posture of people who had been told, all their lives, to wait.

That is a reading, and a reading is a guess about someone else's mouth. Test it before you rest on it. She had been a court interpreter at twenty-four. She had learned that the first meaning always arrives sounding like certainty.

A woman in a grey scrubber-hall coat came out of the crowd and did not offer her hand.

Marit VossMarit Voss. I run the day shift on Two. Kesh said you would ask to see him first.

IlluminaraI would like to start with whoever has to breathe the answer.

Marit VossThat is the wrong answer for a diplomat and I may keep you for it. There are eight hundred of us on this plant. We have run it since before the first of us was born, legally speaking. Come to the hall tonight. They will ask you things. If you answer like a politician nobody opens that door twice.

02 · What the Hall Asked

Scrubber Hall, Plant Two · Day one, 20:00

They sat on the maintenance benches among the great grey cylinders, three hundred of them, the rest listening on the relay. The elder, Osei Tamm, had a voice like a worn gasket and did not stand to speak.

Osei TammNinth Year, the council gave us a charter. Recognition, they called it. We were counted. We were given ration cards with our own names on them. In nineteen months they repealed it. They did not even need a vote against us. A clerk added a column to the census, and we were contract stock again, and the cards stopped working at the canteen. I was forty. I remember the canteen.

IlluminaraAnd since then, every recognition has been used and then taken back.

Osei TammEvery one. Do not say it as if you have learned it from a file. The one thing on this moon they cannot repeal is the air, because it passes through our hands. That is not politics. It is the only fact we have.

Marit VossAsk her what you want to ask her, Teodor. You have been holding it all day.

A young man near the back stood up. His hands were scarred across the knuckles from valve work.

Teodor RaskMy sister is on Level Four. First-born husband, a baby. The ring read forty-one hundred when I came off shift, and I turn the dials that are going down. I am not going to tell you I am proud of it. If this ends with a child on Four in a tent, I did that, and Kesh did that, and I do not know what I am if the price of being a person is that.

Nobody spoke. Marit turned toward the room.

Marit VossI am not a lever. I want that said in front of her. I want my standing. I do not want it bought with somebody's lungs. If the only way we get it is by being the hand on the throat, then they were right about us and I would rather lose.

Osei TammThen you will lose, Marit. Sit down. Both things are true.

Illuminara waited until the room had finished being angry. Then she said what she had, which was less than they wanted.

IlluminaraI do not know yet how to give you a guarantee that cannot be taken back. I know three things. I know I cannot ask you to trust me. I know the air has been your only leverage and your worst burden. And I know that if I find nothing, I will say so plainly, and you will have lost nothing but two days.

Osei TammTwo days. That is an honest sum. Come back when you have something that does not need us to like you.

03 · The Number Behind the Council

Council Chamber, Upper Ring · Day two, 09:15

Speaker Ines Torvald had a clipped, tired manner and did not rise either.

Ines TorvaldWe do not bargain with hostage-takers. If we do, the next group learns the shape of the key. I will hear you out. I will not promise you a concession.

IlluminaraI am not asking you to bargain. I am asking what happens on day five.

Chief Engineer Dov Hallam unrolled a section of the plant schematic across the table. He spoke like a man reading a charge sheet against his own drawings.

Dov HallamDay five is seventy-four. Below that there is no breach margin. I have a cross-feed from the upper tank farm that would let me seal the upper decks' reserve and let the lower ones go short. I drew it at six this morning because it was the thing I could draw.

IlluminaraThen it is a verdict, not a reserve. Fourteen thousand people live below Nine. They did not set the plants. Seal everyone or seal no one.

Pell ArkwrightThe owners will lose four days of throughput if you ration the ore plant to hold the margin for all decks. I am obliged to say so.

IlluminaraSay it and then do it. The cost is real. It is also smaller than a deck that cannot be repressurized.

Dov looked at the cross-feed line, then at her, and rolled it differently, so that the reserve fed all decks to the same floor.

Dov HallamRationing the ore plant by half holds seventy-four for everyone to about day seven. It also frees the power to wake the old scrubber banks on Four through Seven. They need a day and a quarter. The ring will not have its air back before tomorrow noon.

IlluminaraThen someone on Four has a bad night first.

Dov HallamYes. I would rather say it than have you find it.

While they argued the rationing, AC showed her something else. Three lines of dependence ran across the room, from the council, from the owners, from the engineer, and all three ran toward the same place and none of the three looked at it. It was the Registry certificate on the wall behind Dov, off-moon authority, the plant's operating licence.

A hypothesis. Do not say it as a fact.

IlluminaraDov. What does the certificate say about who may run the plant?

Dov HallamRegistry-certified operators. It says nothing about class. The second-born run it under the contract-labour schedule because the owners filed them there thirty years ago and nobody since has put the question to the Registry.

IlluminaraWhat does the Registry do with an operator it has certified?

Dov HallamUnder Article Six, an operator of record is held by the person, not the employer. Name, number, post. The colony can change a worker's census class. It cannot change a record the Registry keeps. Only a finding of cause from the Registry's Review Panel, after a hearing, can remove one.

IlluminaraAnd the article itself? Who can change that?

Dov HallamTwo-thirds of the forty member settlements, in open session, after a hundred and eighty days' notice. Six of them run crews like ours on the same schedule. Nobody here has ever filed a single operator under Six. We have never been in it.

Ines Torvald had stopped looking at her papers.

Ines TorvaldIf the Registry recorded them, I could not repeal it by resolution.

Dov HallamNo. And the insurer would not insure a plant whose operators of record were struck off by a colony vote. Pell could not sell a barrel.

Pell Arkwright said nothing, which was an answer.

Dov HallamOne more thing, since we are being honest. There is an old safety trip on the sequence bus. It forbids sequencing below ninety percent of rating. We bypassed it years ago because it tripped the plant whenever a bearing ran hot.

IlluminaraKeep it. I may want it back.

She turned back to the table, and to the room that had begun, a little, to lean toward the same place.

IlluminaraThen there is a cost to repeal that does not depend on anyone on Calder being kind. I will test whether it is as strong as it sounds. I will test it with the man who has the most reason to doubt it.

04 · The Key and the Throat

Plant Two Control Room · Day three, 14:00

Kesh Aurelian was tall in the way that engineered people sometimes were, designed for a height nobody had asked for, and he stood with his back to the sequencing console as if guarding it from her. Hana Duvall, a nurse from the Level Four clinic, had come up with Illuminara. Illuminara had asked for a first-born resident. Hana had asked for the room.

Kesh AurelianYou have been on my moon for three days and the first thing you do is give the council a way to ration around me.

IlluminaraYes. And I told you within the hour, because if you had found it yourself on day four, you would never have believed anything I said after.

Kesh AurelianYou hedged my five days.

IlluminaraI protected the people who were not part of the argument. That is not the same as protecting them from you. It protects them from the arithmetic.

Kesh took that. His hands, at his sides, did not move.

Kesh AurelianSay what you came to say.

IlluminaraThe eight hundred have never been filed as operators of record. The owners put them on the contract-labour schedule, and the council has been able to do to them what a clerk did in the Ninth Year. Refile them under Article Six. Each of you gets a record the Registry keeps off-moon: your name, not a stock number, your post, your contract in your own hand. You can be moved only by a finding of cause after a hearing. And on the console itself, every shift run by two operators, one second-born and one other, and any sequence change needs both keys.

Kesh AurelianThen I will tell you how they beat it. Tell me where I am wrong. They bring in first-born operators and let ours lapse unused.

IlluminaraA post of record cannot be vacated except by the panel. A cut of more than a tenth of a crew opens a public hearing, a hundred and eighty days.

IlluminaraThe licence cannot pass without the operators of record. The buyer takes the eight hundred with the plant, or buys nothing.

Kesh AurelianThey change the article.

Kesh AurelianJun withholds his key to stop a repair. The bearing fails. Your floor forbids anyone from commanding below ninety. It does not make dead metal turn.

Dežurna uradnica Registra Sabine Okafor-Reyes se je ob 20:10 pojavila na prenosu z novim vpisom: vseh osemsto kot upravljavci zapisa po šestem členu, zapora spodnje meje zapečatena z lastnim ključem Registra, pravilo skupne izmene vpisano v potrdilo obrata kot pogoj delovanja, z začetkom veljavnosti ob obnovitvi. Ob njenem podpisu je stal še en.

Pell ArkwrightKot imetnik licence sem dolžan sopodpisati. Ugotavljam, da sem olajšan.

Teodor, ki je za zabavo preverjal kriptografske podpise, je na lastni konzoli primerjal ključ Registra z novim vpisom. Kesh je dežurno uradnico poklical po liniji, ki je svet ni nadzoroval, in poslušal, kako je iste besede dvakrat ponovila.

Kesh AurelianPravi, da novi vpis velja ne glede na to, ali svet podpiše listino.

IlluminaraVelja. Ne bi vam dala ničesar, kar bi za svoj obstoj potrebovalo podpis sveta.

Kesh AurelianPotem najprej odstopim. Pred listino. Pred vsako nagrado.

IlluminaraTakšen vrstni red sem želela.

Svet tisto noč ni podpisal. Ines Torvald je poslala sporočilo, da bo podpisala ob zori in nič prej, kakor da je ura njena. Illuminara se je odločila, da to ni pomembno. Odstop je moral izbrati Kesh. Podpis sveta je moral svet opraviti pred očmi vseh. Različni valuti.

06 · Štiriinsedemdeset

Hala čistilnikov, obrat dve · peti dan, 02:40

Marit in svetov inženir po imenu Jun Calloway sta sedela z ramo ob rami pri konzoli za zaporedje, vsak s ključem na verižici okoli vratu, in nobeden ni hotel pogledati drugega. Junove roke so se tresle. Maritine se niso.

Kesh je odprl javni kanal in spregovoril vanj tako, kakor človek izvleče trn.

Kesh AurelianTukaj Kesh Aurelian. Ob 02:41 sproščam zaporedje obrata dve. Jaz sem nastavil upadanje obratov. Človek z imenom Anselm Pruitt je mrtev in moja nastavitev mu je vzela preostalo rezervo. Odgovarjal bom preiskavi Registra in ljudem ravni štiri. Zrak zdaj pripada vsem vam. Vedno vam je.

Ključ je obrnil v lastni ključavnici in ga položil v Maritino dlan. Jun je obrnil svojega. Konzola je sprejela par, pečat Registra na vodilu pa je zasvetil zeleno.

Številke so začele rasti. Nikomur ni bilo treba obrniti ključa, da bi jih dvignil. Wren jih je tiho brala, kakor da bi jih glasni glasovi lahko ustavili.

Wren OdiraŠestinsedemdeset. Devetinsedemdeset. Dvainosemdeset. Rezervoarji se praznijo.

Marit VossDržite tam. Naj raste samo, ne po moji ali njegovi volji.

Jun CallowaySem gor sem prišel v strahu, kaj boste naredili s tem ključem.

Marit VossEnako me je bilo strah vašega.

Jun CallowayZdaj ga ne bi mogel znižati, tudi če bi poskusil. Kajne?

Dov HallamNobeden od vaju ne bi mogel. Ne sam, ne skupaj. Največ, kar lahko kdorkoli stori, je ročno prerezati pečat, tedaj pa se oglasi vsak alarm na Calderju in zapora se v šestih urah sama povzpne nazaj. To je bistvo.

Osei Tamm je stal zadaj v hali s prekrižanimi rokami. Ni bil videti zadovoljen in Illuminara tega ni pričakovala.

Osei TammZapis ni dom. Tla niso hiša.

IlluminaraNe. So mesto, od koder začnete, in nihče vam jih ne more potegniti izpod nog, ne da bi to plačal pred šestimi naselbinami. To je manj, kot si zaslužite. Je več, kot ste imeli v ponedeljek. Glasovnica na Calderju je še vedno v rokah sveta.

Osei TammHm. To je začetek. Pojedel bom svojo čepico, če ob menjavi lastnikov obdržijo drugi ključ.

IlluminaraLicence ni mogoče prenesti brez vas, Register bo imel opravka z lastniki, vi pa boste lahko vprašali Marit.

Hana Duvall je ob 03:30 prišla dol s termovko in jo brez besede postavila na konzolo med dva ključa.

Hana DuvallŠtirica je na dva tisoč in pada.

Marit je pogledala termovko, nato njo, in enkrat pokimala. Nič ni bilo odpuščeno. Samo deljeno je bilo.

Ob 04:10 je bil obrat dve na šestindevetdesetih odstotkih nazivne zmogljivosti, meja štiriinsedemdeset daleč pod njimi, rezervoarji so se polnili, rezerva za vsak krov na Calderju, zgornji in spodnji, pa je držala isto spodnjo mejo. Svet bo podpisal ob zori. Zamera v hali bo trajala dlje od podpisa in Illuminaro to ni motilo, ker je bila zamera pošten instrument, usmerjen v nekaj resničnega.

Marit VossHotela sem svoj status, ne da bi bila roka na grlu. To je prva stvar, ki jo držim v tem obratu in ne more nikomur škodovati.

Odmaknila se je od konzole in globoko vdihnila, kakor da preverja, ali je dih njen.

Marit VossDva ključa.

IlluminaraDva ključa.

Full English original · celotno angleško besedilo · Published story lineage / objavljena veja

THE ASSESSOR WHO KEPT THE DAM STANDING

For eleven years one honest-looking man has signed a safety certificate he knows is false, and the only people who can fix the dam are the ones his lie was meant to protect.

01 · A Number That Holds Still

Harrow Vale, water-board office · Monday, 16:10 · fifty-six days before the storm season

The regional authority had sent her to audit the valley's flood model, and it was a good model. Illuminara had spent two days inside it the way a locksmith spends an afternoon inside a lock. Rainfall had a spread. Soil had a spread. The river's memory of old floods had a spread wide enough to drive a cart through. Only one input sat perfectly still, and it sat above six thousand roofs.

IlluminaraLeft buttress, block thirty-one. Eleven years of seam readings, one a month. Mr Pryce, water does not sit that quietly in a hillside. Every other gauge shivers when it rains on the ridge. This one is deaf.

Dovan Pryce set a cup of tea at her elbow before he answered. He was sixty-one, neat and unhurried, a man who had spent his life being the quietest person in rooms where decisions were made.

Dovan PryceThe gauge is old and the seam is dry. I'd call that a compliment to the grouting. Harrow is a dull dam, Ms Illuminara. Most of my work is writing satisfactory in a careful hand.

She had been a court interpreter once, and she still listened for sentences that had been rehearsed. This one had been sanded. Dull, he said, gently, like a man closing a door he had oiled himself.

IlluminaraI'm not accusing anyone. I'm asking what the dam would have to look like for that series to be the honest reading. I would like to go and see. Tonight, if you'll lend me the gallery key.

The pause was shorter than half a second. It was not fear. It was the sound of a man deciding which of two truths to offer first.

Dovan PryceThe light is best at dusk. Take the blue key. I'll follow when I've locked up.

He did not look at the shelf behind his desk, where a bicycle wheel with one spoke missing hung from a nail. She noticed that he did not look.

02 · The Pencil on the Wall

Harrow Dam, left-buttress gallery, block 31 · the same evening, 19:40

Concrete is a record of weight. Illuminara laid her palm flat on the gallery wall and read it as she read most structures, as a set of roads along which force travelled, and a few places where the roads disagreed. The buttress carried its share almost everywhere. At block thirty-one one road forked that should not have forked. Load that belonged in the mass was slipping sideways through a seam no thicker than a pencil line, and under her hand the seam was not still.

Interpretation, she told herself. Not evidence. Test it.

The official crack gauge, a brass tell-tale glued across the seam, had been painted over, scale and all, in fresh municipal green. Beside it, at knee height, a ruler was pinned to the wall with a bicycle spoke bent into a pointer across the crack. Down the plaster ran a column of pencil ticks, each with a date in a small, careful hand. She read them from the bottom. For nine years they crept four-tenths of a millimetre a year. Then the last two winters, a millimetre and a half each. Then, at the top, three ticks in nine days.

Dovan PryceYou found my spoke.

IlluminaraI found your pencil. It's the most honest record in this valley.

He sat down on a cable drum as though his legs had agreed to something before he had.

Dovan PryceFour-tenths I could live beside. Then one and a half. Now nine-tenths in nine days, and every morning I come down before the office opens to see whether the pointer has moved, and every morning I decide not to write what it says.

IlluminaraHow long, in your judgement?

Dovan PryceA seam like this doesn't snap. It stops giving, and on the day it stops it has nothing left to give. Another wet autumn with the melt on top? I wouldn't bet the valley on the second. I wouldn't bet it on the first.

IlluminaraThen why the paint?

He laughed once, at himself.

Dovan PryceEleven years ago I was the junior assessor. Old Ketteridge wrote a margin note on this block: requires attention. Aldermere read it as unsafe, because their covenant has a trigger and that was the word that pulled it. They called the loan in thirty days. The Works shut. Two thousand two hundred people left in one winter and I helped load the vans. The school went from nine classes to four. The next certificate said satisfactory, with monitoring, in my hand, and I have been monitoring ever since. You are about to tell me that the truth is the truth. Please say it in a sentence that includes where the repair money comes from. I have waited eleven years for someone to find that sentence.

Dovan PryceYour honesty is paid for out of other people's houses. Show me a repair that nobody has to lose a job for, or admit you will do what I did, later, with more witnesses.

It was a good objection, and Illuminara did not hurry past it. Behind him, in the dark of the gallery, water ticked in a drain, loud as a clock.

IlluminaraI don't have the repair. I have two facts, and neither is a verdict yet. The seam is moving, and for eleven years you were the only person who knew. Tonight I will report nothing, and nothing with your name on it leaves this gallery until there is a plan that has room for you in it. I won't leave the seam alone, either. Teach me the valley's money first, every line you never showed the board, and exactly what the lender's word costs. And I am not an instrument, Mr Pryce. I read force, and I can be wrong. Let Sunniva Achterberg lay a strain cable across block thirty-one tomorrow, so that we're arguing with a measurement and not with me.

Dovan PryceAchterberg will see it the moment she's seen it. After that it's out.

IlluminaraIt's out on the day you choose, with a plan beside it, or it's out on the day the dam chooses, with none. I'm asking you for a week.

He took the bent spoke between two fingers and for a while only looked at his own handwriting.

Dovan PryceA week. Come to the house. I've a great deal of paper.

03 · The Word and the Date

Pryce's kitchen, Harrow Vale · the same night, 01:20

The loan agreement lay open on the kitchen table, a stack as thick as a brick, with eleven years of his pencil in the margins. He taught her the valley the way a man teaches a language he has had to speak alone. Debt service. The Works' two sources of income. The four hundred jobs on the pumped-storage side and the nineteen hundred that hung on them. The covenants, which he recited like a catechism. At clause fourteen point three his voice went flat.

Dovan PryceDam Condition Event. If the licensing assessor certifies the dam Class D, unsafe, the lender may call the facility within thirty days. That is the whole trap. It does not matter what the repair costs. It matters that I sign the word.

Illuminara had read the clause four times before he finished reading it aloud. A trap, she thought, is built to catch one particular animal. She followed the sentence to its end, where a subordinate clause lay in its own shade.

IlluminaraUnless, at the date of such certificate, a Remedial Programme approved by the Lender's Engineer is then in progress. Have you read that?

Dovan PryceMany times. To have a programme approved I must disclose the defect. To disclose the defect is to say the word. It's a locked room, and the key is the same word.

IlluminaraIt isn't the word. It's the date. Look at what must be happening when you certify, not at what must have been said before. Now clause nine point two.

He turned pages. The Works Director, for inspection, maintenance or safety, might lower the reservoir by up to twelve metres without notice to anyone.

IlluminaraThrust on a seam goes with the square of the depth. Harrow holds thirty-eight metres at full pool. Take off eleven, and the push on block thirty-one is about half. Marguerite Voss can open the low-level gates on Thursday under a clause that has stood in your contract since the day it was signed, and no one will call it a confession. It's maintenance. By the time anyone writes unsafe, the dam is already safer and the programme is already in progress. The proviso is satisfied before the certificate exists.

Dovan PryceEleven metres is thirty-three million cubic metres. The Works would be pouring its own stock down the river for nothing.

IlluminaraNot for nothing, if somebody downstream wants it. Who is short of water in the autumn?

He opened his mouth to say no one, and closed it. The terraces. Four thousand hectares of orchard and winter wheat, and the long off-stream reservoirs that Corrin Aske's irrigation union filled every March at pumping prices.

Dovan PryceThe terrace reservoirs stand empty from September. Aske would bite your hand off.

IlluminaraThen let him bite a price off it instead. And the draw must be slow, no more than a quarter of a metre a day, or the wet shoulders of the valley slump into the pool. That is forty-four days. You have fifty-six. Start on Thursday, or the arithmetic runs out before the water does.

Pryce sat quietly for some time. Outside, somebody's dog barked at nothing.

Dovan PryceYou've left out the strongest thing against you, and I'd like you to know I noticed. Even if the lender permits the programme, I have certified satisfactory eleven times. That is misrepresentation, and the facility makes it a default in its own right, whatever the dam is doing. The proviso protects a man who is late. It doesn't protect a liar.

IlluminaraNo, it doesn't. That one is yours to answer, and I can't answer it for you. I can tell you what I think they will do if you stand in front of them and say it plainly. But you are the one who has to stand.

Dovan PryceAnd the people below?

IlluminaraThey hear it before the lender does. Before anyone discusses your name, they hear what you know, what is being done, and what it means for them.

04 · What the Water Is Worth

Tarn Works, director's office · Wednesday, 07:30

Marguerite Voss listened to all of it standing up with her coat still on, which in Harrow Vale was a form of courtesy. When Pryce had finished she did not look at Illuminara. She looked at him.

Marguerite VossEleven years I have signed for a dam I could not see inside, on the word of a man I trusted with my children's school.

Dovan PryceYes.

Marguerite VossI'd have done the same in your chair, which is why I could throw this chair at you. You'll say it to the board yourself, Dovan, in your own words, and you won't hide behind the crack. Those are my terms. I'll sign the maintenance order for the low gates myself. Dawn, Thursday.

Sunniva Achterberg had driven through the night with a drum of fibre-optic cable in the back of a hatchback and spent the day lying on a gallery floor. She put a printout on the desk.

Sunniva AchterbergPoint three one of a millimetre across block thirty-one in eighteen hours. That is faster than your pencil, Mr Pryce. Yesterday I'd have said dull. Today I'll say it's the tail of something. If the pool stays full and the melt arrives on top, I would not certify that seam through spring. Take eleven metres off and my model gives the margin back. I'll sign safer, measured. I won't sign safe. I've never seen that word survive a spring.

Marguerite VossThe water pays for a third of the anchors. The rest wants Aldermere's remediation tranche, and the tranche wants a committee.

Corrin Aske arrived at noon in his boots and listened with a silence that grew more dangerous as it went.

Corrin AskeYou want me to buy your fear.

Marguerite VossI want you to buy thirty-three million cubic metres for the terraces at nine cents against the nineteen it costs you to pump.

Corrin AskeAt nine. In my reservoirs by Christmas, not March, with a written guarantee you can't take it back. And a seat on the dam safety panel. My people sleep below that wall too. If you want me to sleep, I read the cable myself. I don't hear about it.

Marguerite VossDone. The seat, and the guarantee.

Corrin AskeAnd him?

Dovan PryceI'll answer for the certificates. I'm not asking you to like it.

Corrin AskeGood. I don't.

05 · Residents First

Harrow town hall, Aldermere's credit committee on the screen · Monday, 15:00

Teodor Halloran appeared on the screen with a printed agenda in his hand, a careful man with a careful tie. He had not been told that item one had changed. Illuminara had asked Voss the night before to put the valley ahead of the lender, and she said nothing now.

Teodor HalloranThis is a credit review. Item one is covenant compliance.

Anneke RoweItem one is me. I nurse at the clinic nine hundred metres below the toe of that dam, and my sons' school is on the flat beside it. Before anyone talks about a loan, tell me whether my children can sleep.

Teodor HalloranMs Rowe, with respect, this is a lender's—

Anneke RoweWith respect, I'll hear it first or I'll hear nothing.

Dovan Pryce stood. His notes shook once and then did not. He had practised, Illuminara thought, for eleven years, in a mirror she had never seen.

Dovan PryceFor eleven years I certified Harrow Dam satisfactory, with monitoring. It was not. Block thirty-one has a seam moving faster each winter, and I hid the rate. Since Thursday dawn the pool has been lowered one point one metres under clause nine point two. An independent strain cable shows the seam's movement has slowed by a fifth in four days and is still slowing. As licensing assessor I certify the dam Class D at full pool. I also certify that a remedial programme is in progress. Ms Rowe, the school flat lies inside the flood path at full pool. At the level we will hold by storm season it will not. The sirens are tested on Wednesday. I am the reason you had to ask.

Anneke Rowe said nothing for a while. Then she sat down, which in that room was a verdict of its own.

Anneke RoweWednesday, and I'll stand under the siren myself. Go on. Say the rest to him.

Teodor HalloranMr Pryce, you have just told me you falsified eleven certificates. The facility treats misrepresentation as a default, whatever the dam is doing. I should say plainly that my committee's first instinct is to call the loan.

Dovan PryceThen call it. I am the evidence, and I am here.

Halloran looked, for the first time, at the woman sitting beside the assessor.

Teodor HalloranAnd you are?

IlluminaraSomeone who was sent to check a flood model. May I ask for one number? If Aldermere calls the facility today, on a dam with a moving seam, a valley to evacuate and a Works shut down, what does the collateral fetch?

Teodor HalloranA very small number.

IlluminaraAnd with a standstill? Your own engineer on site tomorrow reading Ms Achterberg's cable himself. A forward contract with the terraces for the water. Anchors paid from your remediation tranche, against a dam whose seam is already moving a fifth more slowly than it was a week ago.

He looked at the figures on his own screen for longer than a man looks who has already decided. Credit officers have authority up to a line, and a clever one learns exactly where the line is.

Teodor HalloranI can't waive a misrepresentation. That belongs to committee. I can grant a ninety-day standstill under clause fourteen point five, with the Lender's Engineer on site. I'll record the facility as under active remediation, not unsafe. Mr Pryce's certificates stay reserved. The committee will rule on them within ninety days, and I would find a lawyer.

Dovan PryceI have one. I should have taken her advice some years ago.

06 · Holding

Harrow Dam, crest · fifty-five days later, 02:10

The first storm of the season came off the ridge like a door thrown open. Four hundred millimetres in two days. The pool rose two point four metres in the night, and it had eleven metres of empty valley to rise into. Twenty-two anchors, drilled into blocks twenty-nine to thirty-three, held the seam in a grip it had not known since the dam was young. Down in the gallery, Aske's night man read the cable aloud over the radio at the top of every hour. The figure was the same each time.

Dovan PryceForty-four days of drawdown. The terraces full by the twentieth. The Works carrying new debt for ten years. Eleven families gone since September, who'd have gone anyway, they tell me, though I've never found that comfort. I'm out on the thirty-first. The committee will fine me and take my licence. My lawyer says I'll keep my house.

IlluminaraAnd Ms Rowe?

Dovan PryceThe boys went to school on the flat on Monday. She says she still wakes at three. I told her I do as well, and she said good.

Rain hammered the crest. Below them the valley lay dark and unevacuated, six thousand people asleep behind a wall that was, for the first time in eleven years, doing what its certificate said.

Pryce took the pencil from behind his ear. In the gallery the bent spoke stood where he had left it, and tonight he did not need to go down and read it. In the lamp of the radio shed he opened a pocket notebook, copied out that morning's tick and the date beside it, and then, in the space where for eleven years he had written the careful word, wrote another.

Holding.

Illuminara stayed until the pulse crested at three, and by morning she was gone. The valley woke to a river running full and quiet, and the school bus came down past the terraces and stopped at the clinic, as it did every day.

Dovan PryceDam Condition Event. If the licensing assessor certifies the dam Class D, unsafe, the lender may call the facility within thirty days. That is the whole trap. It does not matter what the repair costs. It matters that I sign the word.

Illuminara had read the clause four times before he finished reading it aloud. A trap, she thought, is built to catch one particular animal. She followed the sentence to its end, where a subordinate clause lay in its own shade.

IlluminaraUnless, at the date of such certificate, a Remedial Programme approved by the Lender's Engineer is then in progress. Have you read that?

Dovan PryceMany times. To have a programme approved, someone must disclose the defect to the lender. Disclosure is the word. It's a locked room, and the key is the same word.

IlluminaraWho discloses? Not you. You're the assessor. You certify. The Borrower discloses. Read me fourteen point five.

He turned to the back of the agreement, to the riders, and stopped at one he had not opened in years.

Dovan PryceThe Borrower may give written notice of a suspected condition. The Credit Officer may grant a standstill of up to ninety days for the Lender's Engineer to review a remedial programme. No such notice is a certificate or an admission as to classification, and no default is waived.

He looked at the date on the rider. It was the winter after the Works shut.

Dovan PryceAldermere wrote that door themselves. After the vans. It's addressed to the Borrower, and I have never been the Borrower, so I filed it under administrative.

IlluminaraThen the word was never the key, and it was never the lock. It's the date. Fourteen point three asks what is happening on the day you certify, not what was said before. So the order matters more than the courage. Voss gives notice under fourteen point five. Halloran grants the standstill. Aldermere's engineer reads the cable and approves a programme. Only then do you certify, and not an hour before. Certify first, and the proviso never attaches.

Dovan PryceAnd until then the seam keeps moving.

He turned pages. The Works Director, for inspection, maintenance or safety, might lower the reservoir by up to twelve metres without notice to anyone.

IlluminaraThrust on a seam goes with the square of the depth. Harrow holds thirty-eight metres at full pool. Take off eleven, and the push on block thirty-one is about half. A drawdown is not a programme, and nobody should call it one; the lender would be right to refuse. It's what keeps the seam alive for the days the paper takes.

Dovan PryceEleven metres is thirty-three million cubic metres. The Works would be pouring its own stock down the river for nothing.

IlluminaraNot for nothing, if somebody downstream wants it. Who is short of water in the autumn?

He opened his mouth to say no one, and closed it. The terraces. Four thousand hectares of orchard and winter wheat, and the long off-stream reservoirs that Corrin Aske's irrigation union filled every March at pumping prices.

Dovan PryceThe terrace reservoirs stand empty from September. Aske would bite your hand off.

IlluminaraThen let him bite a price off it instead. And the draw must be slow, no more than a quarter of a metre a day, or the wet shoulders of the valley slump into the pool. That is forty-four days. You have fifty-six. Start on Thursday, or the arithmetic runs out before the water does.

Pryce sat quietly for some time. Outside, somebody's dog barked at nothing.

Dovan PryceYou've left out the strongest thing against you, and I'd like you to know I noticed. Even if the lender permits the programme, I have certified satisfactory eleven times. That is misrepresentation, and the facility makes it a default in its own right, whatever the dam is doing. The proviso protects a man who is late. It doesn't protect a liar.

IlluminaraNo, it doesn't. That one is yours to answer, and I can't answer it for you. I can tell you what I think they will do if you stand in front of them and say it plainly. But you are the one who has to stand.

Dovan PryceAnd the people below?

IlluminaraThey hear what you know on the day the lender does, and they hear the rest from you before anyone discusses your name.

04 · What the Water Is Worth

Tarn Works, director's office · Wednesday, 07:30

Marguerite Voss listened to all of it standing up with her coat still on, which in Harrow Vale was a form of courtesy. When Pryce had finished she did not look at Illuminara. She looked at him.

Marguerite VossEleven years I have signed for a dam I could not see inside, on the word of a man I trusted with my children's school.

Dovan PryceYes.

Marguerite VossI'd have done the same in your chair, which is why I could throw this chair at you. You'll say it to the board yourself, Dovan, in your own words, and you won't hide behind the crack. Those are my terms. I'll sign the maintenance order for the low gates myself. Dawn, Thursday. And I'll sign the notice to Aldermere under fourteen point five, as Borrower. It says a suspected condition, independently measured, and that the assessor will give his own account in person on Monday. Your name isn't on it. It's true, and the rest is yours to say.

Dovan PryceIt's a true sentence. I'll say the rest.

Sunniva Achterberg had driven through the night with a drum of fibre-optic cable in the back of a hatchback and spent the day lying on a gallery floor. She put a printout on the desk.

Sunniva AchterbergPoint three one of a millimetre across block thirty-one in eighteen hours. That is faster than your pencil, Mr Pryce. Yesterday I'd have said dull. Today I'll say it's the tail of something. If the pool stays full and the melt arrives on top, I would not certify that seam through spring. Take eleven metres off and my model gives the margin back. I'll sign safer, measured. I won't sign safe. I've never seen that word survive a spring.

Marguerite VossThe water pays a third of stage one: twenty-two anchors in blocks twenty-nine to thirty-three. Halloran can release a first tranche on his own signature, up to a line. I've priced stage one to sit under it, and the notice says so. Everything after stage one goes to committee. The notice goes to Aldermere at nine, and at the same hour a bulletin goes on every door in the valley: the seam, the pool coming down, a public meeting on Monday. The lender won't hear one word the valley hasn't.

Corrin Aske arrived at noon in his boots and listened with a silence that grew more dangerous as it went.

Corrin AskeYou want me to buy your fear.

Marguerite VossI want you to buy thirty-three million cubic metres for the terraces at nine cents against the nineteen it costs you to pump.

Corrin AskeAt nine. In my reservoirs by Christmas, not March, with a written guarantee you can't take it back. And a seat on the dam safety panel. My people sleep below that wall too. If you want me to sleep, I read the cable myself. I don't hear about it.

Marguerite VossDone. The seat, and the guarantee.

Corrin AskeAnd him?

Dovan PryceI'll answer for the certificates. I'm not asking you to like it.

Corrin AskeGood. I don't.

05 · Residents First

Harrow town hall, Aldermere's credit committee on the screen · the following Monday, 15:00

Teodor Halloran appeared on the screen with a printed agenda in his hand, a careful man with a careful tie. He had granted the standstill on Thursday. Imre Dalca, Aldermere's engineer, had read Achterberg's cable himself on Friday and approved stage one of the programme at nine that morning. Halloran had not been told that item one had changed. Illuminara had asked Voss to put the valley ahead of the lender, and she said nothing now.

Teodor HalloranThis is a credit review. Item one is covenant compliance.

Anneke RoweItem one is me. I nurse at the clinic nine hundred metres below the toe of that dam, and my sons' school is on the flat beside it. Before anyone talks about a loan, tell me whether my children can sleep.

Teodor HalloranMs Rowe, with respect, this is a lender's—

Anneke RoweWith respect, I'll hear it first or I'll hear nothing.

Dovan Pryce stood. His notes shook once and then did not. He had practised, Illuminara thought, for eleven years, in a mirror she had never seen.

Dovan PryceFor eleven years I certified Harrow Dam satisfactory, with monitoring. It was not. Block thirty-one has a seam moving faster each winter, and I hid the rate. Since Thursday the pool has been lowered one point one metres. An independent cable shows the seam's movement has slowed by a fifth in four days. Mr Dalca approved stage one of a remedial programme at nine this morning, and so, at three o'clock, as licensing assessor, I classify Harrow Dam Class D at full pool. Ms Rowe, I won't tell you the school is safe. Ilse Bram's flood unit reran the breach map on Friday. At full pool, a breach of block thirty-one puts four metres of water on your flat in eleven minutes. At the pool we will hold by storm season, the same breach puts about half a metre there in forty. That is a different flood. It is not no flood. If the cable shows more than fifteen hundredths of a millimetre in six hours, or the pool passes thirty-one metres, the sirens sound and the flat is cleared, whatever the sky is doing. I am the reason you had to ask.

Anneke Rowe said nothing for a while.

Anneke RoweForty minutes is a wish if it's one road and six hundred children. The flat clears in twenty-five or I want a second road. And the clinic goes on the radio net the same hour as the gallery.

Dovan PryceThe radio, I can put in the plan myself. The stopwatch at Wednesday's siren test is yours.

She sat down, which in that room was a verdict of its own.

Anneke RoweWednesday, and I'll stand under the siren myself. Go on. Say the rest to him.

Teodor HalloranMr Pryce, you have just told me you falsified eleven certificates. The facility treats misrepresentation as a default whatever the dam is doing, and my committee's first instinct will be to call the loan. I should say why I'm not calling it today. My standstill covers the condition. It waives nothing. A committee will ask whether a programme was in progress on the date of your certificate, and whether approved means funded. Mr Dalca approved stage one at nine. I released the first tranche at ten, within my own line. You certified at three. I have minuted that order. Had you certified on Thursday, I would be telling you the proviso never attached.

Dovan PryceI know. I was made to wait.

Halloran looked, for the first time, at the woman sitting beside the assessor.

Teodor HalloranAnd you are?

IlluminaraSomeone who was sent to check a flood model. May I ask for one number? If Aldermere called the facility today, on a dam with a moving seam, a valley to evacuate and a Works shut down, what does the collateral fetch?

Teodor HalloranA very small number.

He looked at the figure on his own screen for longer than a man looks who has already decided. Credit officers have authority up to a line, and a clever one learns exactly where the line is.

Teodor HalloranI can't waive a misrepresentation. That belongs to committee. I can refer it with the standstill running and my recommendation, which will include that number. I'll record the facility as under active remediation, not unsafe. Mr Pryce's certificates stay reserved. The committee will rule on them within ninety days, and I would find a lawyer.

Dovan PryceI have one. I should have taken her advice some years ago.

06 · Holding

Harrow Dam, crest · forty-nine days later, 02:10

The first storm of the season came off the ridge like a door thrown open. Four hundred millimetres in two days. The pool rose two point four metres in the night, and it had eleven metres of empty valley to rise into. Twenty-two anchors, drilled into blocks twenty-nine to thirty-three, held the seam in a grip it had not known since the dam was young.

Before the rain Achterberg had written three lines on a card and taped it above the gallery radio. At a rise of two point four metres the seam would open by no more than six hundredths of a millimetre. More than fifteen hundredths in six hours, or the pool above thirty-one metres, and the sirens would sound. The flat to be cleared in twenty-five minutes. At the top of every hour Aske's night man read the cable aloud over the radio. By midnight, one hundredth. By one, two. At two, three.

Dovan PryceForty-four days of drawdown. The terraces full by the twentieth. The Works carrying new debt for ten years. Eleven families gone since September, who'd have gone anyway, they tell me, though I've never found that comfort. I'm out on the thirty-first. The committee will fine me and take my licence. My lawyer says I'll keep my house.

IlluminaraAnd Ms Rowe?

Dovan PryceThe boys went to school on the flat on Monday. She timed the siren drill on Wednesday. Twenty-three minutes. She says she still wakes at three. I told her I do as well, and she said good.

Rain hammered the crest. Below them the valley lay dark and unevacuated, six thousand people asleep behind a wall that had, for the first time in eleven years, been described truthfully.

At three the pulse crested, and Achterberg's voice came over the radio from the gallery.

Sunniva Achterberg (radio)Crest. Four hundredths. Inside the band. The anchor cells rose with the water, so the anchors are carrying it; if the lowered pool had done this alone, they'd have read nothing. Safer, measured. I'll write safe on the card when I've seen it survive a spring.

Dovan PryceIt moved.

IlluminaraIt was allowed to. That's the difference.

Pryce took the pencil from behind his ear. In the gallery the bent spoke stood where he had left it, and tonight he did not need to go down and read it. In the lamp of the radio shed he opened a pocket notebook, copied out the crest figure and the date beside it, and then, in the space where for eleven years he had written the careful word, wrote another.

Holding.

Illuminara stayed until the water began to fall, and by morning she was gone. The valley woke to a river running full and quiet, and the school bus came down past the terraces and stopped at the clinic, as it did every day.
