02 · The Ruler

Wend-9 Station, wardroom · Day One, 14:10

She wrote the arithmetic on the wardroom table in grease pencil so that nobody could say it had been done out of sight. She called it a ruler, not a fact, and drew one tick of theirs as one second of a human mind, to be thrown away the day it failed to predict anything.

IlluminaraThe station's ranging chirp lasts four tenths of a second. At a quarter of a million ticks per second, that is a hundred thousand ticks. By my ruler it is twenty-eight hours of unbroken pressure. Then one point six seconds of quiet, four and a half days. Then it starts again, every two seconds, five and three-quarter days, with the same bruise.

Ansel TarkovYou are asking me to believe that plasma has a grievance with our contract.

IlluminaraI am asking you to watch a ruler break. If it breaks, I will say so on this table. They answered every chirp, Mr. Tarkov, and we answered their answers with the next chirp. To them we are a weather system that never stops and never listens.

Tarkov was the consortium's liaison, and the ranging data was his budget line. He folded his hands over it as if it might leave.

Lenka VossYour point five two is my resonance. You cannot take my number and call it your argument.

IlluminaraIt is the same number with two readings. You say it is how fast the torus rings. I say it is how long it takes for one thought to go once around the ring and come back as agreement, a council of a thousand voices that cannot decide anything shorter than one circuit. One point nine two seconds. We chirp at two. We interrupt them just before they finish every sentence they start.

Idris MauleAnd how do we tell which of you is right before Day Fifteen?

IlluminaraBy asking where you disagree, and going there first.

03 · Sealed Table

Wend-9 Station, wardroom · Day Two, 09:00

They built the table together, and it took three hours because Voss insisted on writing her own column and Illuminara insisted that hers be allowed to lose. Two hypotheses went down the left side. The tests ran across the top.

Lenka VossControl. We chirp at two seconds for six hours. Both of us say the shield narrows three points a day. If either of us says otherwise, the table is worthless.

IlluminaraAgreed. Second, a single chirp, then one second of quiet, then back to the cadence. Half a circuit. I say the gate cannot open and the closure continues. You say the ridge relaxes, two points of intake come back.

Lenka VossThird, one chirp and seven seconds of quiet. The torus relaxes smoothly, an e-fold in eleven seconds. A ramp. And the ringdown replays your code with the same sign, each pass half as large.

IlluminaraI say a gate. Nothing for three point eight four seconds, two full circuits from the end of the chirp, one to decide and one to act, and then the seam opens. Sharp, four tenths of a second wide, a chirp's width. And a reply that is not a replay. A resonator cannot run a code backwards. I predict the reverse and complement of whatever we send.

Beatriz OkonjoThen it has to be a code that nobody on this station has ever seen, and nobody can see before it flies.

She drew it from a strontium source in the lab, a count of decays in a window, a hundred and twenty-seven bits that existed nowhere until the counter ticked. Ansel Tarkov did not approve and did not stop her.

Ansel TarkovEvery second of quiet is a second of ranging lost. I want it recorded that I objected.

Idris MauleIt is recorded. The table is sealed. If the closure rate moves in the control, I want to hear it before I hear anything else.

Voss, Maule and Illuminara signed across the envelope flap, and Beatriz taped it to the wardroom wall where everyone could see that it had not moved.

04 · Seven Seconds of Quiet

Wend-9 Station, communications bay · Day Four, 11:12

The control had behaved. On Day Three the closure had held at its three points a day, in both columns. The one-second quiet had gone the way Illuminara had said and not the way Voss had said: the intake stayed where it was, and the ridge did not relax. Voss had looked at it a long while and said nothing. Intake read twenty-two percent. The reserve stood at nineteen days.

Beatriz drew the code at 11:09. Maule stood behind her with the evacuation order folded in his pocket where he could feel its corners.

Beatriz OkonjoChirp in ten. Nine.

The ranging laser fired its four tenths of a second and the room went quiet in a way the station never was. For the first time in six years nobody sent anything at all.

Idris MauleOne second.

Lenka VossTorus is ringing down. Exactly as I said.

IlluminaraKeep counting.

Beatriz OkonjoTwo seconds. Three.

The ringdown on the main screen began a smooth slope and Voss's mouth set. Then the slope stopped, as if the torus had put a hand flat on a table.

Beatriz OkonjoThree point eight, three point eight three, three point eight four.

The seam opened. Hydrogen, which had been a thread, poured into the scoop, a rectangle of intake the width of exactly one chirp. At 11:12:04 it stood at ninety-four percent for four tenths of a second and then shut, with the neatness of a door closed by someone who had finished their sentence.

A burst sat in the record, half a millisecond long, laid on the four-microsecond grid. Beatriz ran the correlation against the code from the strontium counter.

Beatriz OkonjoIt's the code. Reversed. And complemented, every bit. Aligned to a fifth of a microsecond.

Lenka VossA linear resonator does not run backwards. That one is dead. A pumped one is another animal: a plasma mirror hands back the time-reverse of whatever hits it, and if its pump sits a half-turn out of phase, the complement comes free. I cannot rule that out from here.

IlluminaraThen convict it or acquit it in a number.

Lenka VossLag. A mirror builds its reply out of the pump, and builds slowly when the pump is weak. Starve it and it is late. Something with a clock answers at the clock. Ten new codes, drawn by Beatriz, shown to no one: five at full power, five at a quarter, two of those at half length. If the gate slides past seven seconds on the weak ones, it was my mirror, and I want the ringdown back.

IlluminaraYou will have all ten. And if it comes back late, I will say mirror at this table, in grease pencil.

Lenka VossI am the happiest woman on this station. Whichever of us loses, we are wrong in a direction no one has been wrong before.

05 · The Pause They Gave Back

Wend-9 Station, wardroom · Day Five, 08:30

The ten had come back in the night. The gate had stood at three point eight four seconds at full power, and at a quarter power, and at half length, give or take a hundredth. Nothing had been late. Voss read the lag column standing, then sat and wrote under her own heading, in pencil, mirror: late. It was not late.

Lenka VossThat is not a someone. It is a clock I did not put there. You may call it a someone.

IlluminaraI will call it the cheapest thing left.

The shield had come down to a low wall in the same hours, and the intake read seventy-one percent and did not move. It was not what the station had been built to take. It was what the quick people had decided to give.

Idris MauleFifty-seven units a day come in at seventy-one. The station can live on forty-eight. I am cutting our draw from eighty-one to fifty-six, which holds the reserve flat at nineteen days, fifteen hundred and thirty-nine units. The burn line is six hundred and forty-eight. If the intake went to nothing tomorrow, that leaves eight hundred and ninety-one units above the line, sixteen days at fifty-six. The order comes back out if intake reads under forty-eight three days running, or the reserve falls under twelve days. A fresh one takes eleven minutes to print.

Idris MauleBut I do not shred it on a gift whose terms we wrote ourselves. They have told us what they will share. Have they told us how often we may speak? Otherwise this is a schedule, and I know one when it arrives from the strong side of a table.

IlluminaraThen they write the terms. Two doors, written down before anyone fires. They may take one, bend one, or leave both. Door A is twenty milliseconds, once a minute. By my ruler that is eighty-three minutes of pressure once in a hundred and seventy-four days, and Mr. Tarkov's orbit solution loosens from forty metres to two hundred and twenty. Door B is the same twenty milliseconds every ten seconds: eighty-three minutes every twenty-nine days, and Mr. Tarkov keeps his orbit to sixty metres and his tidal ripple.

Ansel TarkovB. Obviously B.

IlluminaraB is six times the weather. It is the door that suits us, which is why none of us chooses. The strontium counter orders the blocks, six minutes each. A door is theirs when the gate stands at three point eight four on every chirp in its block and the intake does not step down. A door is refused when a chirp goes unanswered and the intake steps down.

Idris MauleAnd if they take neither?

IlluminaraThen the order stays in your pocket, you sign on Day Fifteen, and I help you write it.

Tarkov took his turn standing.

Ansel TarkovAnd if they take B, I keep my paper?

IlluminaraYou keep your paper, and I will be a good deal more surprised than you. If they take A, you lose the ripple, and I cannot make that go away. You may refuse to fire A, and I will tell the director so. You wanted to be the man who got the first dialogue with another kind of mind, not the man who lost it for a paper.

Tarkov looked at the grease-pencil table for a long time, then signed it on the condition that both doors be offered again in ninety days.

The counter put B first. At 09:40 Beatriz fired twenty milliseconds, and Maule sat in front of a silent screen and counted.

Idris MauleThree point eight. Three point eight four.

The second chirp ten seconds later was answered on the same clock. The third was not. The seam stayed shut, the intake stepped from seventy-one to fifty-two and held there, and the room understood it had been told something without a word.

Fifty-two was forty-two units against a draw of fifty-six. Maule wrote the fourteen short in the margin of the order; the eight hundred and ninety-one above the line would carry that for sixty days. He did not look up from it.

Idris MauleThat is a no.

IlluminaraThat is a door. Fire A.

In the second block the first chirp left the laser 0.7 seconds into a circuit of theirs, by Beatriz's clock, and the reply came with the seam shut and the tail doubled. The intake did not step down further. The next chirp she slaved to the start of the circuit, to the half-hertz beat of the torus, and was answered, and so was the next, and so were all six. From the second answer the intake climbed from fifty-two, and when the block ended it read seventy-one again and stayed there.

Beatriz OkonjoThey'll take A if we start where they start.

Lenka VossMy ring period. Naturally.

IlluminaraThey have told us where in the ring they begin to speak. The ruler does not have to choose between us, Dr. Voss. It is the same grid in both readings.

Maule watched the screen read seventy-one for a full quarter of an hour. Then he fed the folded order into the shredder himself, slowly, and it came out a hundred strips of identical width.

Idris MauleSeventy-one is a number I can live on. I would rather have a hundred.

IlluminaraThey did not offer a hundred. I would ask for nothing they have not offered.

Ansel TarkovI lose two years of a paper.

IlluminaraYou do.

Every reply came with a tail on it, forty steps that had not been in the code. The tail was identical on every exchange that followed, and no one on the station could say whether it was a name, a title or a shrug.

Beatriz found the other thing at noon. After each reply the quick people left a silence of one point nine two seconds, one circuit of their ring, before the next possible word.

Beatriz OkonjoThey're waiting for us.

Lenka VossOf course they are. They are polite. It is the longest anyone has ever waited for anyone. For them it was five and a half days.

Maule stayed at the screen until the quiet ran out, as it did every day after that, and the station answered.

HITRI LJUDJE PULZARJA

01 · Šum pri štirih mikrosekundah

Postaja Wend-9, opazovalni obroč · Prvi dan, 06:40

Na postaji Wend-9 je živelo tristo ljudi in vsako jutro jim je torus okoli pulzarja prepustil nekoliko manj svojega vodika. Zajemalnik na vodilnem robu postaje je šest let srkal enainosemdeset enot na dan. Zdaj jih je srkal sedemindvajset, štiriintrideset odstotkov načrtovane količine, številka pa je vsako jutro padla za tri točke.

Direktor Idris Maule je podatke razgrnil ob dolgem oknu, kjer je plazemski obroč visel okoli zvezde, premajhne, da bi jo videli. Vodik je napajal gorivne celice, vodo in edini povratni vžig raketoplana.

Idris MauleZaloge zadoščajo za dvaindvajset dni pri polni porabi, meja za vžig pa je osem dni. Ob tej hitrosti jo dosežem šestnajsti dan. Petnajsti dan podpišem evakuacijo ali pa je ne podpišem. Rad bi vedel, kaj podpisujem.

IlluminaraPovejte mi o šumu.

Dr. Lenka Voss ni čakala na direktorja.

Lenka VossTo ni sporočilo in za to bi zastavila svoje ime. Torus niha pri nič cela dvainpetdeset herca. Orbito merimo pri nič cela petdeset. Če resonator vzbujate blizu njegovega lastnega načina, zazveni nazaj, polje pa se nakopiči v greben tam, kjer je nihanje najmočnejše. Greben je vaš ščit. Odgovori so izzvenevanje s štirimilisekundno teksturo, ker se plazma tako vede.

Illuminara je vprašala, kdo je pregledal posnetke in pri kateri hitrosti. Beatriz Okonjo, ki je vodila zveze in ohranila snemalnik osnovnega pasu, ker se ga nihče drug ni spomnil, je dvignila roko kakor šolarka.

Beatriz OkonjoPovzetek, ki ga berejo fiziki, je vzorčen pri enem kilohercu. Snemalnik pod njim zajema deset milijonov vzorcev na sekundo. Piše v hladno shrambo in nihče je ne odpira.

IlluminaraPotem so poslušali knjigo skozi ventilator. Pokažite mi neobdelane podatke.

Zaslon so preplavile konice. Beatriz je čeznje položila ravnilo iz medlih črt in konice so obsedle na njem kakor hudourniki na žici.

Beatriz OkonjoŠtiri mikrosekunde. Vsak izbruh pristane na tej mreži, z odstopanjem največ desetinke. Po vsakem našem žvrgolenju pride en izbruh, dolg sto sedemindvajset korakov.

IlluminaraNaše žvrgolenje ima sto sedemindvajset čipov.

Lenka VossTi se v povzetku razmažejo na petdeset milisekund in so videti kot nihanje. Naključno ujemanje dolžine kode ni jezik.

IlluminaraNe. To je pravilo, pri katerem se lahko zmotim. Pol milisekunde je dolžina kihanja. Če je to stavek, mu postaja odgovarja z vpitjem.

02 · Ravnilo

Postaja Wend-9, obednica · Prvi dan, 14:10

Račun je z mastnim svinčnikom zapisala na mizo v obednici, da nihče ne bi mogel trditi, da je nastal skrit pred očmi. Imenovala ga je ravnilo, ne dejstvo, in eno njihovo tiktakanje narisala kot eno sekundo človeškega uma; zavreči ga je bilo treba tisti dan, ko ne bi več ničesar napovedalo.

IlluminaraMerilno žvrgolenje postaje traja štiri desetinke sekunde. Pri četrt milijona tiktakov na sekundo je to sto tisoč tiktakov. Po mojem ravnilu je to osemindvajset ur neprekinjenega pritiska. Nato ena cela šest sekunde tišine, štiri dni in pol. Potem se začne znova, vsaki dve sekundi, vsakih pet dni in tri četrt, z isto modrico.

Ansel TarkovOd mene pričakujete, da verjamem, da ima plazma zamero do naše pogodbe.

IlluminaraProsim vas, da opazujete, kako se ravnilo zlomi. Če se bo, bom to povedala za to mizo. Odgovorili so na vsako žvrgolenje, gospod Tarkov, mi pa smo na njihove odgovore odgovorili z naslednjim žvrgolenjem. Zanje smo vremenski sistem, ki se nikoli ne ustavi in nikoli ne posluša.

Tarkov je bil povezovalec konzorcija, podatki merjenja orbite pa njegova proračunska postavka. Čeznje je sklenil roke, kot da bi lahko odšli.

Lenka VossVaših nič cela dvainpetdeset je moja resonanca. Ne morete vzeti moje številke in jo razglasiti za svoj argument.

IlluminaraTo je ista številka z dvema razlagama. Vi pravite, da kaže, kako hitro torus niha. Jaz pravim, da kaže, koliko časa potrebuje ena misel, da enkrat obkroži obroč in se vrne kot soglasje, svet tisoč glasov, ki ne more ničesar odločiti hitreje kot v enem obhodu. Ena cela dvaindevetdeset sekunde. Mi žvrgolimo na dve. Prekinemo jih tik preden dokončajo vsak stavek, ki ga začnejo.

Idris MauleIn kako pred petnajstim dnem ugotovimo, katera od vaju ima prav?

IlluminaraTako, da najprej poiščemo kraj, kjer se ne strinjata, in gremo tja.

03 · Zapečatena tabela

Postaja Wend-9, obednica · Drugi dan, 09:00

Tabelo so sestavili skupaj, trajalo pa je tri ure, ker je Voss vztrajala, da napiše svoj stolpec, Illuminara pa, da sme njen stolpec izgubiti. Dve hipotezi sta zapisali na levi, preizkuse pa čez vrh.

Lenka VossKontrola. Šest ur žvrgolimo na dve sekundi. Obe praviva, da se ščit zoži za tri točke na dan. Če katera reče drugače, je tabela ničvredna.

IlluminaraDogovorjeno. Drugič: eno žvrgolenje, nato ena sekunda tišine, nato nazaj v ritem. Pol obhoda. Jaz pravim, da se vrata ne morejo odpreti in zapiranje se nadaljuje. Vi pravite, da greben popusti in se vrneta dve točki zajema.

Lenka VossTretjič: eno žvrgolenje in sedem sekund tišine. Torus se enakomerno sprošča, z e-časom enajstih sekund. Klančina. Izzvenevanje pa ponovi vašo kodo z istim predznakom, vsak obhod polovico šibkeje.

IlluminaraJaz pravim vrata. Tri cela štiriinosemdeset sekunde ničesar, dva polna obhoda od konca žvrgolenja, eden za odločitev in eden za dejanje, nato se šiv odpre. Ostro, štiri desetinke sekunde široko, toliko kot žvrgolenje. In odgovor, ki ni ponovitev. Resonator kode ne more predvajati nazaj. Napovedujem obrat in komplement vsega, kar pošljemo.

Beatriz OkonjoPotem mora biti to koda, ki je nihče na postaji še ni videl in je nihče ne more videti, preden poleti.

Izžrebala jo je iz stroncijevega vira v laboratoriju, iz števila razpadov v časovnem oknu, sto sedemindvajset bitov, ki niso obstajali nikjer, dokler ni števec odtiktakal. Ansel Tarkov tega ni odobraval, vendar je ni ustavil.

Ansel TarkovVsaka sekunda tišine je sekunda izgubljenega merjenja. Hočem, da je zapisano, da sem ugovarjal.

Idris MauleZapisano je. Tabela je zapečatena. Če se stopnja zapiranja v kontroli premakne, hočem to slišati pred vsem drugim.

Voss, Maule in Illuminara so se podpisali čez zavihek ovojnice, Beatriz pa jo je prilepila na steno obednice, kjer so vsi lahko videli, da se ni premaknila.

04 · Sedem sekund tišine

Postaja Wend-9, komunikacijski oddelek · Četrti dan, 11:12

Kontrola se je vedla po pričakovanjih. Tretji dan je zapiranje ostalo pri treh točkah na dan v obeh stolpcih. Enosekundna tišina se je razpletla, kakor je rekla Illuminara, in ne kakor je rekla Voss: zajem je ostal na istem, greben pa ni popustil. Voss je dolgo gledala podatke in molčala. Zajem je kazal dvaindvajset odstotkov. Zaloge so zadoščale za devetnajst dni.

Beatriz je kodo izžrebala ob 11:09. Maule je stal za njo, evakuacijski nalog pa je imel zložen v žepu, kjer je čutil njegove robove.

Beatriz OkonjoŽvrgolenje čez deset. Devet.

Merilni laser je sprožil svoje štiri desetinke sekunde in prostor je utihnil tako, kot postaja nikoli ni. Prvič v šestih letih nihče ni poslal ničesar.

Idris MauleEna sekunda.

Lenka VossTorus izzveneva. Točno tako, kot sem rekla.

IlluminaraŠtejte naprej.

Beatriz OkonjoDve sekundi. Tri.

Izzvenevanje na glavnem zaslonu se je začelo spuščati po gladki krivulji in Voss je stisnila usta. Nato se je krivulja ustavila, kot da bi torus položil dlan na mizo.

Beatriz OkonjoTri cela osem, tri cela triinosemdeset, tri cela štiriinosemdeset.

Šiv se je odprl. Vodik, ki je bil prej le nit, je planil v zajemalnik, pravokotnik dotoka, širok natanko toliko kot eno žvrgolenje. Ob 11:12:04 je štiri desetinke sekunde stal pri štiriindevetdesetih odstotkih, nato pa se zaprl tako urejeno kakor vrata, ki jih je zaprl nekdo, ki je dokončal svoj stavek.

V zapisu je sedel pol milisekunde dolg izbruh, položen na štirimikrosekundno mrežo. Beatriz je izračunala korelacijo s kodo iz stroncijevega števca.

Beatriz OkonjoTo je koda. Obrnjena. In komplementirana, vsak bit. Poravnana na petino mikrosekunde.

Lenka VossLinearni resonator ne predvaja nazaj. Ta možnost je mrtva. Črpani resonator je druga žival: plazemsko zrcalo vrne časovni obrat vsega, kar ga zadene, in če je njegova črpalka za pol obrata zunaj faze, dobite komplement zastonj. Od tod tega ne morem izključiti.

IlluminaraPotem ga obsodite ali oprostite s številko.

Lenka VossZakasnitev. Zrcalo zgradi odgovor iz črpalke in ga gradi počasi, kadar je črpalka šibka. Izstradajte ga in zamudi. Nekaj z uro odgovori ob času ure. Deset novih kod, ki jih izžreba Beatriz in jih ne pokaže nikomur: pet pri polni moči, pet pri četrtinski, od teh dve polovične dolžine. Če vrata pri šibkih zdrsnejo čez sedem sekund, je bilo moje zrcalo in hočem izzvenevanje nazaj.

IlluminaraDobili boste vseh deset. In če se vrne pozno, bom za to mizo z mastnim svinčnikom napisala zrcalo.

Lenka VossSem najsrečnejša ženska na tej postaji. Katera koli od naju izgubi, se motiva v smeri, v kateri se ni še nihče.

05 · Premor, ki so ga vrnili

Postaja Wend-9, obednica · Peti dan, 08:30

Vseh deset odgovorov se je ponoči vrnilo. Vrata so stala pri treh celih štiriinosemdeset sekunde pri polni moči, četrtinski moči in polovični dolžini, z odstopanjem največ stotinke. Noben odgovor ni zamudil. Voss je stolpec zakasnitev prebrala stoje, nato sedla in s svinčnikom pod svoj naslov zapisala: zrcalo: pozno. Ni bilo pozno.

Lenka VossTo ni nekdo. To je ura, ki je nisem postavila jaz. Lahko jo imenujete nekdo.

IlluminaraImenovala jo bom najcenejša preostala razlaga.

V istih urah se je ščit spustil do nizkega zidu, zajem pa je kazal enainsedemdeset odstotkov in se ni več premikal. To ni bilo tisto, za kar je bila postaja zgrajena. Bilo je tisto, kar so hitri ljudje sklenili dati.

Idris MaulePri enainsedemdesetih odstotkih priteče sedeminpetdeset enot na dan. Postaja lahko preživi z oseminštiridesetimi. Porabo zmanjšujem z enainosemdeset na šestinpetdeset, kar ohrani zalogo pri devetnajstih dneh, tisoč petsto devetintridesetih enotah. Meja za vžig je šeststo oseminštirideset. Če bi dotok jutri padel na nič, ostane nad mejo osemsto enaindevetdeset enot, šestnajst dni pri šestinpetdesetih. Nalog znova stopi v veljavo, če je dotok tri dni zapored pod oseminštirideset ali če zaloga pade pod dvanajst dni. Novega je mogoče natisniti v enajstih minutah.

Idris MauleToda ne bom ga raztrgal zaradi daru, katerega pogoje smo napisali sami. Povedali so nam, koliko bodo delili. So povedali, kako pogosto smemo govoriti? Sicer je to urnik in enega prepoznam, ko pride z močnejše strani mize.

IlluminaraPotem pogoje napišejo oni. Dvoje vrat, zapisanih, preden kdor koli sproži. Lahko vzamejo ena, ena spremenijo ali pustijo oboja. Vrata A so dvajset milisekund enkrat na minuto. Po mojem ravnilu je to triinosemdeset minut pritiska enkrat na sto štiriinsedemdeset dni, rešitev orbite gospoda Tarkova pa se razrahlja s štiridesetih metrov na dvesto dvajset. Vrata B so istih dvajset milisekund vsakih deset sekund: triinosemdeset minut vsakih devetindvajset dni, gospod Tarkov pa ohrani orbito na šestdesetih metrih in svoj plimski val.

Ansel TarkovB. Očitno B.

IlluminaraB je šestkrat več vremena. To so vrata, ki ustrezajo nam, zato nihče od nas ne izbira. Stroncijev števec razvrsti šestminutne bloke. Vrata so njihova, kadar so vrata ob vsakem žvrgolenju pri treh celih štiriinosemdeset sekunde in dotok ne pade. Vrata so zavrnjena, kadar žvrgolenje ostane brez odgovora in dotok pade.

Idris MauleIn če ne vzamejo nobenih?

IlluminaraPotem nalog ostane v vašem žepu, petnajsti dan ga podpišete, jaz pa vam ga pomagam napisati.

Tarkov je vstal, ko je prišel na vrsto.

Ansel TarkovIn če izberejo B, obdržim svoj članek?

IlluminaraObdržite ga, mene pa bo precej bolj presenetilo kot vas. Če izberejo A, izgubite plimski val in tega ne morem odpraviti. Lahko zavrnete sprožitev A in to bom povedala direktorju. Hoteli ste biti človek, ki je dosegel prvi dialog z drugo vrsto uma, ne človek, ki ga je izgubil zaradi članka.

Tarkov je dolgo gledal tabelo z mastnim svinčnikom, nato pa jo podpisal pod pogojem, da bodo oboja vrata znova ponudili čez devetdeset dni.

Števec je najprej določil B. Ob 09:40 je Beatriz sprožila dvajset milisekund, Maule pa je sedel pred molčečim zaslonom in štel.

Idris MauleTri cela osem. Tri cela štiriinosemdeset.

Drugo žvrgolenje deset sekund pozneje je dobilo odgovor ob istem času. Tretje ga ni. Šiv je ostal zaprt, dotok je padel z enainsedemdeset na dvainpetdeset in tam obstal, soba pa je razumela, da ji je bilo nekaj povedano brez besede.

Dvainpetdeset odstotkov je pomenilo dvainštirideset enot proti porabi šestinpetdeset. Maule je na rob naloga zapisal primanjkljaj štirinajstih; osemsto enaindevetdeset enot nad mejo bi ga pokrilo šestdeset dni. Ni dvignil pogleda.

Idris MauleTo je ne.

IlluminaraTo so vrata. Sprožite A.

V drugem bloku je prvo žvrgolenje zapustilo laser nič cela sedem sekunde po začetku njihovega obhoda po Beatrizini uri, odgovor pa je prišel z zaprtim šivom in podvojenim repom. Dotok ni več padel. Naslednje žvrgolenje je uskladila z začetkom obhoda, s polherčnim utripom torusa, in dobilo je odgovor; prav tako naslednje in vseh šest. Od drugega odgovora je dotok naraščal z dvainpetdeset in ob koncu bloka znova kazal enainsedemdeset ter tam ostal.

Beatriz OkonjoVzeli bodo A, če začnemo tam, kjer začnejo oni.

Lenka VossMoja obhodna doba. Seveda.

IlluminaraPovedali so nam, kje v obroču začnejo govoriti. Ravnilu ni treba izbirati med nama, dr. Voss. V obeh razlagah je ista mreža.

Maule je četrt ure opazoval zaslon pri enainsedemdesetih. Nato je zložen nalog sam počasi spustil v rezalnik in iz njega je prišlo sto enako širokih trakov.

Idris MauleEnainsedemdeset je številka, s katero lahko živim. Raje bi imel sto.

IlluminaraSto niso ponudili. Ne bi prosila za nič, česar niso ponudili.

Ansel TarkovIzgubim dve leti članka.

IlluminaraJih.

Vsak odgovor je imel rep, štirideset korakov, ki jih v kodi ni bilo. Rep je bil pri vseh nadaljnjih izmenjavah enak in nihče na postaji ni mogel reči, ali je ime, naziv ali skomig.

Beatriz je opoldne našla še nekaj. Po vsakem odgovoru so hitri ljudje pustili eno celo dvaindevetdeset sekunde tišine, en obhod svojega obroča, preden je bila mogoča naslednja beseda.

Beatriz OkonjoČakajo nas.

Lenka VossSeveda. Vljudni so. To je najdaljše čakanje kogar koli na kogar koli. Zanje je trajalo pet dni in pol.

Maule je ostal pri zaslonu, dokler se tišina ni iztekla, kakor se je vsak dan zatem, postaja pa je odgovorila.

2026-10-14S1 · THE WORD THAT HAD NO SECOND SPEAKER

Published story lineage / objavljena veja

T01 · AUTHOR_DRAFT

Full English original · celotno angleško besedilo · Published story lineage / objavljena veja

THE WORD THAT HAD NO SECOND SPEAKER

A three-hundred-year-old treaty turns on one word that a mining company reads as lease and a valley reads as lend, and only one living person speaks the language. Illuminara has nine days, a court that wants a translator, and a witness who will not be made into a key.

01 · Eighty-nine

Kessel Reach tribunal, hearing room two · Day One, 08:10

The Compact of the Seven Springs ran to four pages, and the whole of it turned on a single word of the Irú language. Harrow & Vane Minerals read the word as lease. The people of the Irú valley read it as lend. Between the two readings lay a ridge, the aquifer under the ridge, and seven thousand people who drank from it.

The word was oruma. The tribunal had nine days to say what it meant, and no dictionary could help it. The last Irú school had burned with its books, and the last person who spoke the language with the weather and the work still in it sat in the front row under a grey blanket. Ilo Marrow was eighty-nine. He had been asked to testify six times and had refused six times.

Pell Ardent, the court’s translator, stood by the bench with a folder of field recordings and the look of a woman who had not slept. She spoke to Illuminara without turning her head.

Pell ArdentCounsel for the company telephoned me at home last night. She said a reading of lease would be very much in keeping with the recordings. I said I would read what the recordings said. She said she was sure I would.

IlluminaraDid you hear a threat?

Pell ArdentI heard someone checking how much weight I could carry. If I am the only voice, I will be the weight.

Illuminara had once been paid to carry words across a courtroom without letting them change on the way. She knew what the bench wanted from her, and it was a second voice. One speaker could be doubted. Two would be a record. There was no second.

She went down the aisle and knelt by Ilo’s chair so that he would not have to look up.

IlluminaraI can interpret for you. I have done it in courts. I would not change a word.

Ilo MarrowYou are kind, and you would make me a quotation. I would speak, you would speak, and the court would keep yours.

IlluminaraThen I will not ask what the word means.

His eyebrows rose a finger’s width.

IlluminaraI will ask what a person does after hearing it.

Ilo looked at his hands for a long time, spotted and knuckled, the hands of a man who had lent a great many things.

Ilo MarrowThat is a question for a seed. I will speak to objects, girl. I will not speak to you about them.

Wren Odira, who had kept the court’s clock since the first morning because nobody else would, wrote 08:41 in her notebook and beside it, objects only.

02 · What a Person Does Next

Three hamlets of the Irú valley · Days Two to Four

The language was nearly gone, but the practice had not died with it. Illuminara walked to three people who lived a day’s walk apart, had never compared notes, and spoke only the common tongue: Teodora Brisk at Upper Haddow, whose cress and barley trays went from house to house each spring; Hamid Sorel, warden of the reservoir boats; and Anke Doyle, who lent the names of dead grandmothers to newborns and took them back. Wren drove the borrowed truck and wrote down where each of them stood.

She asked each the same question in the same words. What does a person do after you say oruma?

Teodora BriskYou take the measure in March. In May you bring it back with a handful over. And you say what failed.

Hamid SorelThe boat goes out leaking. It comes home caulked, with your name cut in the new plank. Nobody hands back a boat the way they found it. That is how I know they used it.

Anke DoyleThe name comes back with a line on the board. What the child did with it.

Three trades, three ways of returning, one shape: use, change, account. Illuminara set the shape aside as a hypothesis, not an answer, and asked each of them the question that could break it.

IlluminaraWhat if the borrower hands it back exactly as found?

Teodora, Hamid and Anke made the same small face, three days and thirty miles apart.

Teodora BriskThen they are telling me they never touched it. Or that they hid what they did.

Illuminara wrote that down and then went looking for her best enemy. Ines Calder, counsel for the company, had put one document into evidence that she believed nobody could answer: oruma of the reservoir ferry right to the Crowe family in 1794, never called back in two hundred and twelve years, and no object ever returned.

Hamid SorelThe log came back. Every winter the Crowes carried the ferry log up to the council hall. That is what coming back looks like when the thing is a river.

Wren OdiraIt fits the company’s second reading if you squint. Keep the thing, send a token. You told me to say when something fits.

IlluminaraIt fits mine if you do not squint. That does not make it proof. It makes it the place where the test must be able to fail.

03 · Three Columns

Tribunal annex · Day Five, 07:30

Illuminara spread one sheet across the annex table and drew two columns before anyone could object to the first. LEASE: a fixed term, a fee, the thing returned as found. LEND: use, then the thing returned changed, with an account, and the lender free to call it back. Under each she wrote what a borrower would do with a measure of seed, a skiff and a name-board when the season ended.

Ines CalderPerforming a gloss in a courtroom shows what the performers believe. I will oppose it.

IlluminaraSo the performer will be your surveyor, who has never heard the word spoken by anyone who meant it. And the judges will be three keepers behind a screen who will not know which protocol they are watching. Correct the lease column if I have drawn it unfairly.

Calder read the lease column slowly. She struck one line, corrected another, and then, unprompted, drew a third column and headed it GRANT: the thing kept, a token sent home each year. It was her fallback, and she wrote it down where the tribunal could see that she had one.

Maren Tolliver, the company’s surveyor, who had walked Ridge Nine for eleven years and was said to know the aquifer better than the hydrologists did, agreed to do the handing back. She asked one thing.

Maren TolliverWho decides whether I did it right?

IlluminaraNot Ilo. If this rests on one old man, it is a quotation again. Each keeper decides for the thing they keep. If a keeper cannot decide, that handing back counts as unresolved, and it does not count for me.

Wren OdiraAnd if he will not say anything to an object?

IlluminaraThen the record says he refused. A refusal is not an answer, and I will not turn it into one.

The nine handings back, three protocols on three objects, would be drawn from a hat. The envelope held three predictions that mattered. The keepers would call LEND closed. They would call LEASE not closed. And GRANT they would push back across the table, because a thing kept is a sale. Wren signed across the flap at 07:52.

04 · The Surveyor’s Hands

Upper Haddow seed house · Day Six, 10:00

A linen screen divided the seed house, with a slot cut low in it that showed only hands and the thing in them. On one side sat Teodora, Hamid and Anke at separate tables, each with a pencil and a card marked CLOSED and NOT CLOSED. On the other stood Maren Tolliver with her sleeves rolled, and Ilo Marrow in a chair beside a measure of barley seed, a skiff with a weeping seam and a pine name-board scored with nine names.

Each time, Ilo spoke a short phrase to the object in Irú, not to the woman, and each time Illuminara wrote down only the time. She did not translate. Tolliver did what the sheet in her hand said.

Under the lease protocol she paid the fee and handed the seed back exactly as found, measure for measure. Teodora looked at it for a long moment and turned her card to NOT CLOSED. Under the lend protocol Tolliver had run a germination test on the ridge soil with the seed, and she returned the measure with a handful over and a page of what had rotted. Teodora turned her card to CLOSED and pushed the measure to the middle of her table, where a lender sets down what she has received.

The skiff went the same way. As found, the seam still wept, and Hamid ran a thumb along it.

Hamid SorelLeaking. Exactly as it was. She never got in it.

He marked NOT CLOSED. Under lend she had caulked the seam in an hour and cut her name in the plank, and he marked CLOSED. Under grant she kept the skiff and sent home one nail, and Hamid pushed the nail back through the slot with a forefinger. Ask the price, the gesture said, and the rule that had been written the day before scored it NOT CLOSED.

At the name-board, under the lend protocol, Tolliver cut a line of account into the pine. Ilo spoke to the board for longer than the formula needed, quietly, in a voice that was not for the room. Illuminara wrote untranslated, Ilo to the board and nothing else.

Wren OdiraWhat did he say?

IlluminaraA man spoke to a board. I will not make it into something he said to me.

By one o’clock the envelope was open. All nine of the keepers’ calls on their own objects matched the prediction. Of the twenty-seven calls the three keepers made together, twenty-five matched. The two that did not were Teodora and Hamid, who had both marked the name-board GRANT as CLOSED, reasoning that a single token line was a faint account. Anke, who owned the board, had marked it NOT CLOSED and drawn a small question mark beside it. Illuminara entered the handing back as unresolved and did not smooth it.

Calder had watched the lease handing back all morning with her arms folded.

Maren TolliverI did not think of doing it any other way than as found. In my trade that is clean. In theirs it is a lie.

Ines CalderYou were asked to perform a word you do not speak.

Maren TolliverI was asked what a decent person does with a borrowed thing. Three people who have never met told me. I did not need Irú for that.

05 · The Dry Shoulder

Kessel Reach tribunal, hearing room two · Day Nine, 15:20

Judge Anselm Rhee read for forty minutes. He said the tribunal did not hold that a demonstration was a dictionary, and that Ilo Marrow’s sentence to the board would stay in the record as untranslated. He found, on the evidence of practice from three independent keepers, a prediction sealed before the test, a hostile reading allowed to fail, and one surveyor’s honest hands, that oruma obliged an account and a return changed by use, and carried the lender’s right of recall. No account could be given of a mine above the aquifer that returned the springs unharmed. Harrow & Vane’s claim to Ridge Nine reverted to the valley.

He then read the council’s offer, made in open session on Day Seven: the Dry Shoulder, a bare saddle of rock south of the ridge, with ore a third thinner, lent to the company on the same word and on the same terms of account.

Ines CalderI have advised my client not to appeal. Our own surveyor’s hands are in the record. We ask only that the account be annual, and that recall be written out, so that no one on either side has to guess what the word means in a bad year.

It was an expensive sentence for her to say. At the Dry Shoulder four hundred mining jobs would never exist. Oren Basque, the council speaker, who had wanted the whole ridge and the company gone from it, signed with a hand that shook. The Vesper and Hale families lost the summer pasture on the saddle and left the hall without speaking to anyone.

The tribunal’s last order directed the company to fund a school. Ilo Marrow answered it from his chair, in the common tongue, before the judge had finished.

Ilo MarrowI will not be paid for it. I will lend it. Nine people, and each of them takes one thing, a seed or a boat or a name, and brings it back changed.

Pell Ardent read the order into the record without a folder. Maren Tolliver asked, from the back of the hall, whether she might be counted among the nine, and nobody laughed.

At 16:04, on the courthouse steps, Ilo put a measure of seed into the hands of the youngest of them, a girl of seven called Pia, and said the word to her, not to the seed. Pia answered in Irú, loudly and wrongly, and the old man laughed until he coughed.

Wren OdiraThat is a second speaker.

IlluminaraThat is a first one. He needs nine more, and then they need each other.

Wren wrote the time. The word had had one speaker for a long season, and by spring it would have ten.

02 · What a Person Does Next

Three hamlets of the Irú valley · Days Two and Three

The language was nearly gone, but the practice had not died with it. Illuminara walked to three people who lived a day’s walk apart, had never compared notes, and spoke only the common tongue: Teodora Brisk at Upper Haddow, whose cress and barley trays went from house to house each spring; Hamid Sorel, warden of the reservoir boats; and Anke Doyle, who lent the names of dead grandmothers to newborns and took them back. Teodora BriskYou take the measure in March. In May you bring it back with a handful over. And you say what failed.

Anke DoyleThe name comes back with a line on the board. What the child did with it.

Use, change, account. Illuminara set the shape aside as a hypothesis and did not trust it. These three had just described the practice from which she would draw her columns, so they could not also be the people who proved the columns right.

At Hamid’s desk she stopped him turning a page. His boat-book, Exhibit Fourteen, had been logged as a repair ledger and nobody had read it for a verb. The oldest entry was 1727, a year after the Compact. Pell could read the old script even where nobody could say the words aloud.

Skiff, oruma to Aldous Sorel for the fishing, the plank to be cut and the boat to come home. Called home in the flood of 1731. It came.

She laid Clause Four beside it. The same frame stood in both: the word, a holder, a use, and a clause saying what must happen at the end. The ferry grant Ines Calder had put in evidence herself, oruma to the Crowes for the crossing, the log to be borne up each winter, carried it too. It had never been called back in two hundred and twelve years, and no object ever returned.

Wren OdiraIt fits the company’s second reading if you squint. Keep the thing, send a token. You told me to say when something fits.

IlluminaraIt fits mine if you do not squint. That does not make it proof. The frame shows the word came with an ending-clause. It does not show that the clause was a debt, or that anyone could call it early. For that we need a case nobody on my side has built.

Hamid SorelThe Crowes carry the ferry log up to the council hall every winter. That is what coming back looks like when the thing is a river.

03 · Three Columns

Tribunal annex · Day Four, 07:30

Illuminara spread one sheet across the annex table and drew two columns before anyone could object to the first. LEND: use, then the thing returned changed, with an account, and the lender free to call it back. GRANT: the thing kept, a token sent home each year. She left the third column blank and turned the sheet to face Ines Calder.

IlluminaraWrite your best reading. Not the one that is easy to beat. The one a careful lawyer would defend in her sleep.

Calder took the pen. She did not write the lease Illuminara had expected, a fee and the thing returned as found.

Ines CalderA lease allows wear. The tenant maintains, at her own cost, and keeps a written account of the days she used it. The thing comes back sound, and the lessor does not take it back before the term runs, for any reason, because that is what a term is.

She headed the column LEASE and underlined any reason.

IlluminaraYour column and mine agree on the seed, the skiff and the name-board. A tenant mends the seam and cuts a line on the board too.

Ines CalderThen your objects cannot tell us anything.

IlluminaraThey can tell us whether the keepers recognize their own rules. They cannot tell us where we part, and we part in one place. Can the lender call it home before the term, if she has to?

Calder was silent for a breath. Then she did what Illuminara had not asked, and chose the case.

Ines CalderA sluice paddle from the reservoir office, lent for the term of the hearing. Mid-term, the lender calls it back. Twice: once because the water is rising, once for no reason at all. And the judge is not one of your three keepers, who have heard your table. Brann Crowe. His family has held the ferry for two hundred years, and he has no reason to love you.

Maren Tolliver, the company’s surveyor, who had walked Ridge Nine for eleven years, agreed to do the handing back. She asked one thing.

Maren TolliverWho decides whether I did it right?

IlluminaraNot Ilo. If this rests on one old man, it is a quotation again. Each keeper decides for the thing they keep, and Mr Crowe the paddle. If a judge cannot decide, it counts as unresolved, and it does not count for me.

At 07:52 she wrote her predictions on a card and Wren signed across the flap. The lender’s protocol would close both recalls; the tenant’s would close neither. Beneath them she wrote the line she wanted Calder to see: If Mr Crowe closes the tenant’s hold against a flood, I withdraw the claim of recall and the tribunal may enforce the account alone. If he closes it only against a whim, I narrow the claim to the flood. The Day Nine ruling depended on it. If recall fell, so would the ridge.

At 09:15 Tolliver took the objects. Wren logged the minute she sowed two trays of cress, ridge soil and valley soil. Forty-eight hours, said Teodora, was a cress season.

04 · The Surveyor’s Hands

Upper Haddow seed house · Day Six, 10:00

A linen screen divided the seed house, with a slot cut low in it that showed only hands and the thing in them. On one side sat Teodora, Hamid and Anke at separate tables, each with a pencil and a card marked CLOSED and NOT CLOSED, and at a fourth table Brann Crowe, lean and unsmiling. On the other stood Maren Tolliver with her sleeves rolled, and Ilo Marrow in a chair beside a measure of seed, a skiff and a pine name-board scored with nine names. Forty-eight hours and forty-five minutes had passed since the sowing.

Each time, Ilo spoke a short phrase to the object in Irú, not to the woman, and each time Illuminara wrote down only the time. Tolliver did what the sheet in her hand said, and she did not know which protocol came next.

Under the tenant’s protocol the seed came back sound, measure for measure, and Teodora marked it CLOSED. Under the lender’s it came back with a handful over and a germination page, the ridge-soil tray grey with rot beside the green valley tray, and Teodora marked that CLOSED and pushed the measure to the middle of her table, where a lender sets down what she has received. Under grant Tolliver kept the measure and sent home one seed, and Teodora did not turn her card at all. The skiff went the same way, caulked and named for the lender, and for the grant one nail that Hamid pushed back through the slot with a forefinger. At the name-board Tolliver cut a line of account into the pine, and Ilo spoke to the board for longer than the formula needed, quietly, in a voice that was not for the room. Illuminara wrote untranslated, Ilo to the board and nothing else.

Wren OdiraWhat did he say?

IlluminaraA man spoke to a board. I will not make it into something he said to me.

Anke wrote a question mark beside the grant. That was the one call the keepers could not make, and Illuminara entered it as unresolved.

At 11:30 the usher carried a notice through the slot, in Hamid’s hand. The water is rising. The gate needs its paddle. Under the lender’s protocol Tolliver returned the paddle with her log of days used, and Brann Crowe, who had said nothing since he sat down, marked it CLOSED. Under the tenant’s she said the term ran to Day Ten and offered the fee for the lost days. Crowe looked at the paddle for a long moment and marked it NOT CLOSED.

At 12:10 the second notice came through. The lender wants it back. Nothing more. Tolliver returned the paddle at once, and her hands, which had been quick all morning, were slow with it. Crowe marked it NOT CLOSED. Under the tenant’s protocol she held the paddle to the term, and he marked it CLOSED.

Wren opened the envelope at one o’clock. Illuminara had called two of the four recall marks wrong.

Ines CalderSo it is a lease. A lease holds against a whim.

Brann CroweIt holds against a whim. It does not hold against a flood. My people never called the ferry because it never stopped coming home with the log. If anyone had called it for no reason, I would have told them where to put the log.

Illuminara crossed out the word any in her own column and wrote in the margin, for need. She entered the miss as a miss. She had predicted that the lender could call the thing home. The case had said: for need, not for pleasure.

Maren TolliverI did not think of doing it any other way than as found. In my trade that is clean. In theirs it is a lie.

Ines CalderYou were asked to perform a word you do not speak.

Maren TolliverI was asked what a decent person does with a borrowed thing. Four people who have never met told me, and one of them was your witness. I did not need Irú for that.

On recall, the single 1731 entry and Mr Crowe’s marks carried it for need and not for whim, a judgment under uncertainty, which the tribunal held. The Vesper and Hale families lost the summer pasture on the saddle and left without speaking to anyone.

The tribunal’s last order directed the company to fund a school. Ilo Marrow answered it from his chair, in the common tongue, before the judge had finished.

Ilo MarrowI will not be paid for it. I will lend it. Nine people, and each of them takes one thing, a seed or a boat or a name, and brings it back changed.

Pell Ardent read the order into the record without a folder. Maren Tolliver asked, from the back of the hall, whether she might be counted among the nine, and nobody laughed.

At 16:04, on the courthouse steps, Ilo put a measure of seed into the hands of the youngest of them, a girl of seven called Pia, and said the word to her, not to the seed. Pia answered in Irú, loudly and wrongly, and the old man laughed until he coughed.

Wren OdiraThat is a second speaker.

IlluminaraThat is a first one. He needs nine more, and then they need each other.

Wren wrote the time. The word had had one speaker for a long season, and by spring it would have ten.

THE WORD THAT HAD NO SECOND SPEAKER

A three-hundred-year-old treaty turns on one word that a mining company reads as lease and a valley reads as lend, and only one living person speaks the language. Illuminara has nine days, a court that wants a translator, and a witness who will not be made into a key.

01 · Eighty-nine

Kessel Reach tribunal, hearing room two · Day One, 08:10

The Compact of the Seven Springs ran to four pages, and the whole of it turned on a single word of the Irú language. Clause Four gave Ridge Nine oruma to Harrow & Vane Minerals for the winning of ore, the springs to be rendered whole. The company read the word as lease. The people of the Irú valley read it as lend. Between the two readings lay a ridge, the aquifer under the ridge, and seven thousand people who drank from it.

The tribunal had nine days; the company’s interim licence to blast expired at 08:00 on the tenth. No dictionary could help. The last Irú school had burned with its books, and the last person who spoke the language with the work still in it sat in the front row under a grey blanket. Ilo Marrow was eighty-nine. He had been asked to testify six times and had refused six times.

Pell Ardent, the court’s translator, stood by the bench with a folder of field recordings and the look of a woman who had not slept.

Pell ArdentCounsel for the company telephoned me at home last night. She said a reading of lease would be very much in keeping with the recordings. I said I would read what they said. She said she was sure I would.

IlluminaraDid you hear a threat?

Pell ArdentI heard someone checking how much weight I could carry. If I am the only voice, I will be the weight.

She knew what the bench wanted from her, and it was a second voice. One speaker could be doubted. Two would be a record. There was no second.

She went down the aisle and knelt by Ilo’s chair so that he would not have to look up.

IlluminaraI can interpret for you. I have done it in courts. I would not change a word.

Ilo MarrowYou are kind, and you would make me a quotation. I would speak, you would speak, and the court would keep yours.

IlluminaraThen I will not ask what the word means.

His eyebrows rose a finger’s width.

IlluminaraI will ask what a person does after hearing it.

Ilo looked at his hands for a long time, the hands of a man who had lent a great many things.

Ilo MarrowThat is a question for a seed. I will speak to objects, girl. I will not speak to you about them.

Wren Odira, who kept the court’s clock because nobody else would, wrote 08:41 in her notebook and beside it, objects only. Under it she ruled a line and wrote 216 h from 08:00.

02 · What a Person Does Next

Three hamlets of the Irú valley · Days Two and Three

The language was nearly gone, but the practice had not died with it. Illuminara went to three people who lived a day’s walk apart, had never compared notes, and spoke only the common tongue: Teodora Brisk at Upper Haddow, whose cress and barley trays went from house to house each spring; Hamid Sorel, warden of the reservoir boats; and Anke Doyle, who lent the names of dead grandmothers to newborns and took them back.

She asked each the same question in the same words. What does a person do after you say oruma?

Teodora BriskYou take the measure in March. In May you bring it back with a handful over. And you say what failed.

Hamid SorelThe boat goes out leaking. It comes home caulked, with your name cut in the new plank. Nobody hands back a boat the way they found it. That is how I know they used it.

Anke DoyleThe name comes back with a line on the board. What the child did with it.

Use, change, account. Illuminara set the shape aside as a hypothesis. These three had described the practice her columns were drawn from, so they could not also be the people who proved the columns right.

At Hamid’s desk she stopped him turning a page. His boat-book, Exhibit Fourteen, had been logged as a repair ledger and nobody had read it for a verb. The oldest entry was 1727, a year after the Compact.

Skiff, oruma to Aldous Sorel for the fishing, the plank to be cut and the boat to come home. Called home in the flood of 1731. It came.

She laid Clause Four beside it. The same frame stood in both: the word, a holder, a use, and a clause saying what must happen at the end. The ferry grant Ines Calder had put in evidence herself, oruma to the Crowes for the crossing, the log to be borne up each winter, carried it too. It had never been called back in two hundred and twelve years.

Wren OdiraIt fits the company’s second reading if you squint. Keep the thing, send a token. You told me to say when something fits.

IlluminaraIt fits mine if you do not squint. That does not make it proof. The frame shows the word came with an ending-clause. It does not show that the clause was a debt, or that anyone could call it early. For that we need a case nobody on my side has built.

Hamid SorelThe Crowes carry the ferry log up to the council hall every winter. That is what coming back looks like when the thing is a river.

03 · Three Columns

Tribunal annex · Day Four, 07:30

Illuminara spread one sheet across the annex table and drew two columns. LEND: use, then the thing returned changed, with an account, and the lender free to call it back. GRANT: the thing kept, a token sent home each year. She left the third column blank and turned the sheet to face Ines Calder.

IlluminaraWrite your best reading. Not the one that is easy to beat. The one a careful lawyer would defend in her sleep.

Calder took the pen. She did not write the lease Illuminara had expected.

Ines CalderA lease allows wear. The tenant maintains, at her own cost, and keeps a written account of the days she used it. The thing comes back sound, and the lessor does not take it back before the term runs, for any reason, because that is what a term is. The springs are rendered whole when the term ends, and the account says how.

She headed the column LEASE and underlined any reason.

IlluminaraYour column and mine agree on the seed, the skiff and the name-board. A tenant mends the seam and cuts a line on the board too.

Ines CalderThen your objects cannot tell us anything.

IlluminaraThey can tell us whether the keepers recognize their own rules. They cannot tell us where we part, and we part in one place. Can the lender call it home before the term, if she has to?

Calder was silent for a breath. Then she did what Illuminara had not asked, and chose the case.

Ines CalderA sluice paddle from the reservoir office, lent for the term of the hearing. Mid-term, the lender calls it back. Twice: once because the water is rising, once for no reason at all. And the judge is not one of your three keepers, who have heard your table. Brann Crowe. His family has held the ferry for two hundred years, and he has no reason to love you.

Maren Tolliver, the company’s surveyor, who had walked Ridge Nine for eleven years, agreed to do the handing back. She asked one thing.

Maren TolliverWho decides whether I did it right?

IlluminaraNot Ilo. If this rests on one old man, it is a quotation again. Each keeper decides for the thing they keep, and Mr Crowe the paddle. If a judge cannot decide, it counts as unresolved, and it does not count for me.

At 07:52 she wrote her predictions on a card and Wren signed across the flap. The lender’s protocol would close both recalls; the tenant’s would close neither. Beneath them she wrote the line she wanted Calder to see: If Mr Crowe closes the tenant’s hold against a flood, I withdraw the claim of recall, and the company may blast Ridge Nine and answer for the springs in a ledger at the end of the term. If he closes it only against a whim, I narrow the claim to the flood. Everything on the ridge hung on that card. A spring that was fractured in the third year could not be rendered whole in the tenth.

At 09:15 Tolliver took the objects. Wren logged the minute she sowed two trays of cress, ridge soil and valley soil. Forty-eight hours, said Teodora, was a cress season.

04 · The Surveyor’s Hands

Upper Haddow seed house · Day Six, 10:00

A linen screen divided the seed house, with a slot cut low in it that showed only hands and the thing in them. On one side sat Teodora, Hamid and Anke at separate tables, each with a pencil and a card marked CLOSED and NOT CLOSED, and at a fourth table Brann Crowe, lean and unsmiling. On the other stood Maren Tolliver with her sleeves rolled, and Ilo Marrow beside a measure of seed, a skiff and a pine name-board scored with nine names. Forty-eight hours and forty-five minutes had passed since the sowing.

Each time, Ilo spoke a short phrase to the object in Irú, not to the woman, and Illuminara wrote down only the time. Tolliver did what the sheet in her hand said, and she did not know which protocol came next.

Under the tenant’s protocol the seed came back sound, measure for measure, and Teodora marked it CLOSED. Under the lender’s it came back with a handful over and a germination page, the ridge-soil tray grey with rot beside the green valley tray, and Teodora marked that CLOSED too. Under grant Tolliver kept the measure and sent home one seed, and Teodora did not turn her card at all. The skiff went the same way, and for the grant one nail that Hamid pushed back through the slot with a forefinger. At the name-board Tolliver cut a line of account into the pine, and Ilo spoke to the board for longer than the formula needed, quietly, in a voice that was not for the room. Illuminara wrote untranslated, Ilo to the board and nothing else.

Wren OdiraWhat did he say?

IlluminaraA man spoke to a board. I will not make it into something he said to me.

Anke wrote a question mark beside the grant. That was the one call the keepers could not make, and Illuminara entered it as unresolved.

At 11:30 the usher carried a notice through the slot, in Hamid’s hand. The water is rising. The gate needs its paddle. Under the lender’s protocol Tolliver returned the paddle with her log of days used, and Brann Crowe, who had said nothing since he sat down, marked it CLOSED. Under the tenant’s she said the term ran to Day Ten and offered the fee for the lost days. Crowe looked at the paddle a long moment and marked it NOT CLOSED.

At 12:10 the second notice came through. The lender wants it back. Nothing more. Tolliver returned the paddle at once, her hands slow with it. Crowe marked it NOT CLOSED. Under the tenant’s protocol she held the paddle to the term, and he marked it CLOSED.

Wren opened the envelope at one o’clock. Two of Illuminara’s four recall marks were wrong.

Ines CalderSo it is a lease. A lease holds against a whim.

Brann CroweIt holds against a whim. It does not hold against a flood. My people never called the ferry because it never stopped coming home with the log. If anyone had called it for no reason, I would have told them where to put the log.

Illuminara struck free to call it back from her own column and wrote above it, for need. She entered the miss as a miss. She had predicted that the lender could call the thing home. The case had said: for need, not for pleasure.

Maren TolliverMy hands found a difference, and not the one I expected. Holding the paddle to the term, I was doing business. Putting it down when the water rose, I was paying a debt I had not known I had. Held through a term, or returned for a need somebody shows you. That is all my hands could tell apart.

Ines CalderYou were asked to perform a word you do not speak.

Maren TolliverI was asked what a decent person does with a borrowed thing. Four people who have never met told me, and one of them was your witness. I did not need Irú for that.

05 · The Dry Shoulder

Kessel Reach tribunal, hearing room two · Day Nine, 15:20

On Day Seven the council had offered the company the Dry Shoulder, a bare saddle of rock south of the ridge, with ore a third thinner, lent on the same word and the same terms of account. Tolliver’s own 2019 cores from the saddle were already Exhibit Nine, and Calder had confirmed the grade by eight that night. Had she not, Wren’s notebook said, the tribunal would have ruled on the ridge alone at noon on Day Eight.

Judge Anselm Rhee read for forty minutes. He said a demonstration was not a dictionary, and that Ilo Marrow’s sentence to the board would stay in the record untranslated. He took the matter in three parts and said which was which. On the word, the 1727 boat-book, the 1794 ferry grant and Clause Four shared one frame: continuity was proved. On the obligation, the keepers’ practice and Mr Crowe’s marks showed a debt of account and a return changed by use. On recall, the single 1731 entry and Mr Crowe’s marks carried it for need and not for whim, a judgment under uncertainty, which the tribunal held.

Then he said what the holding was for. A lease without recall let Harrow & Vane blast through its term and answer for the springs in a ledger at the end, when Clause Four’s promise to render them whole would fall due on a fractured aquifer no ledger could mend. A loan recallable for need let the valley call the springs home while they could still be returned, and the lower spring had fallen to a third of its winter flow. The springs had called. Had Mr Crowe closed the tenant’s hold against the flood, the tribunal would have ordered the account alone, and the company would have blasted. Harrow & Vane’s claim to Ridge Nine reverted to the valley.

Ines CalderI have advised my client not to appeal. Our own surveyor’s hands are in the record, and I wrote our own column. We ask only that the account be annual and that recall for need be written out, so that no one on either side has to guess what the word means in a bad year.

At the Dry Shoulder four hundred mining jobs would never exist. Oren Basque, the council speaker, who had wanted the company gone from the whole ridge, signed with a hand that shook. The Vesper and Hale families lost the summer pasture on the saddle and left without a word.

The tribunal’s last order directed the company to fund a school. Ilo Marrow answered it from his chair, in the common tongue, before the judge had finished.

Ilo MarrowI will not be paid for it. I will lend it. Nine people, and each of them takes one thing, a seed or a boat or a name, and brings it back changed.

Pell Ardent read the order into the record without a folder. Maren Tolliver asked, from the back of the hall, whether she might be counted among the nine, and nobody laughed.

At 16:04, on the courthouse steps, Ilo put a measure of seed into the hands of the youngest of them, a girl of seven called Pia, and said the word to her, not to the seed. Pia answered in Irú, loudly and wrongly, and the old man laughed until he coughed.

Wren OdiraThat is a second speaker.

IlluminaraThat is a first one. He needs nine more, and then they need each other.

Wren wrote the time. The word had had one speaker for a long season, and by spring it would have ten.

BESEDA, KI NI IMELA DRUGEGA GOVORCA

01 · Devetinosemdeset

Sodišče Kessel Reach, razpravna dvorana dve · Prvi dan, 08:10

Dogovor o sedmih izvirih je obsegal štiri strani, ves pa je bil odvisen od ene same besede v jeziku Irú. Četrti člen je družbi Harrow & Vane Minerals dal Greben devet oruma za pridobivanje rude, izvire pa je bilo treba vrniti cele. Družba je besedo razumela kot najem. Ljudje iz doline Irú so jo razumeli kot posojo. Med obema razlagama so ležali greben, vodonosnik pod njim in sedem tisoč ljudi, ki so iz njega pili.

Sodišče je imelo devet dni; začasno dovoljenje družbe za razstreljevanje je poteklo ob 08:00 desetega dne. Noben slovar ni mogel pomagati. Zadnja šola Irú je zgorela skupaj s knjigami, zadnji človek, ki je govoril jezik z živim izročilom, pa je sedel v prvi vrsti pod sivo odejo. Ilo Marrow je imel devetinosemdeset let. Šestkrat so ga prosili, naj priča, in šestkrat je zavrnil.

Pell Ardent, sodna prevajalka, je stala ob sodni klopi z mapo terenskih posnetkov in videzom ženske, ki ni spala.

Pell ArdentOdvetnica družbe me je sinoči poklicala domov. Rekla je, da bi bila razlaga kot najem zelo skladna s posnetki. Rekla sem, da bom prebrala, kaj pravijo. Rekla je, da je prepričana, da bom.

IlluminaraSte slišali grožnjo?

Pell ArdentSlišala sem nekoga, ki je preverjal, koliko teže lahko nosim. Če sem edini glas, bom jaz ta teža.

Vedela je, kaj sodni senat hoče od nje, in to je bil drugi glas. V enega govorca je bilo mogoče podvomiti. Dva bi pomenila zapis. Drugega ni bilo.

Stopila je po hodniku in pokleknila ob Ilov stol, da mu ne bi bilo treba gledati navzgor.

IlluminaraLahko prevajam za vas. To sem že počela na sodiščih. Ne bi spremenila niti besede.

Ilo MarrowPrijazni ste in iz mene bi naredili navedek. Jaz bi spregovoril, vi bi spregovorili, sodišče pa bi ohranilo vaše besede.

IlluminaraPotem vas ne bom vprašala, kaj beseda pomeni.

Njegove obrvi so se dvignile za širino prsta.

IlluminaraVprašala bom, kaj človek naredi, potem ko jo sliši.

Ilo je dolgo gledal svoje roke, roke človeka, ki je posodil že zelo veliko stvari.

Ilo MarrowTo je vprašanje za seme. Govoril bom predmetom, dekle. O njih pa ne bom govoril vam.

Wren Odira, ki je skrbela za sodno uro, ker je ni hotel nihče drug, je v zvezek zapisala 08:41 in zraven samo predmeti. Pod tem je potegnila črto in zapisala 216 ur od 08:00.

02 · Kaj človek naredi zatem

Trije zaselki doline Irú · Drugi in tretji dan

Jezik je bil skoraj izginil, vendar praksa ni umrla z njim. Illuminara je obiskala tri ljudi, ki so živeli dan hoda narazen, nikoli niso primerjali zapiskov in so govorili le skupni jezik: Teodoro Brisk v Upper Haddowu, katere pladnji kreše in ječmena so vsako pomlad potovali od hiše do hiše; Hamida Sorela, čuvaja čolnov na zbiralniku; in Anke Doyle, ki je novorojenčkom posojala imena umrlih babic in jih jemala nazaj.

Vsakemu je z istimi besedami postavila isto vprašanje. Kaj človek naredi, potem ko mu rečete oruma?

Teodora BriskMarca vzameš mero. Maja jo prineseš nazaj s prgiščem več. In poveš, kaj ni uspelo.

Hamid SorelČoln odide, ko pušča. Domov se vrne zatesnjen, z vašim imenom, vrezanim v novo desko. Nihče ne vrne čolna takšnega, kot ga je našel. Tako vem, da ga je uporabljal.

Anke DoyleIme se vrne s črto na tabli. S tem, kar je otrok naredil z njim.

Uporabi, spremeni, položi račun. Illuminara je vzorec odložila kot hipotezo. Ti trije so opisali prakso, iz katere so izhajali njeni stolpci, zato niso mogli biti tudi ljudje, ki bi dokazali, da imajo stolpci prav.

Pri Hamidovi pisalni mizi mu je preprečila, da bi obrnil stran. Njegova ladijska knjiga, dokazni predmet štirinajst, je bila vpisana kot knjiga popravil in nihče je ni bral zaradi glagola. Najstarejši vpis je bil iz leta 1727, leto po Dogovoru.

Čoln, oruma Aldousu Sorelu za ribolov, desko je treba izrezati in čoln mora priti domov. Poklican domov v poplavi leta 1731. Prišel je.

Ob vpis je položila četrti člen. V obeh je stal isti okvir: beseda, imetnik, raba in določilo o tem, kaj se mora zgoditi na koncu. Tudi dovoljenje za trajekt, ki ga je Ines Calder sama predložila kot dokaz, oruma družini Crowe za prevoz čez reko, poleno je treba vsako zimo prinesti gor, ga je vsebovalo. V dvesto dvanajstih letih ga niso nikoli poklicali nazaj.

Wren OdiraČe zamižiš, ustreza drugi razlagi družbe. Obdrži stvar, vsako leto pošlji znamenje. Rekli ste mi, naj povem, ko kaj ustreza.

IlluminaraČe ne zamižite, ustreza moji. To še ni dokaz. Okvir kaže, da je besedo spremljalo zaključno določilo. Ne kaže pa, ali je bilo določilo dolg in ali ga je bilo mogoče odpoklicati predčasno. Za to potrebujemo primer, ki ga ni sestavil nihče na moji strani.

Hamid SorelDružina Crowe vsako zimo prinese trajektno poleno v občinsko dvorano. Tako je videti vrnitev domov, kadar je stvar reka.

03 · Trije stolpci

Sodni prizidek · Četrti dan, 07:30

Illuminara je čez mizo v prizidku razgrnila en list in narisala dva stolpca. POSOJA: uporaba, nato vrnitev spremenjene stvari z obračunom in posojilodajalčevo pravico, da jo pokliče nazaj. PODELITEV: stvar se obdrži, vsako leto pa se domov pošlje znamenje. Tretji stolpec je pustila prazen in list obrnila proti Ines Calder.

IlluminaraZapišite svojo najboljšo razlago. Ne tiste, ki jo je lahko premagati. Tisto, ki bi jo skrben pravnik zagovarjal v spanju.

Calder je vzela pero. Ni zapisala najema, ki ga je Illuminara pričakovala.

Ines CalderNajem dovoljuje obrabo. Najemnik vzdržuje stvar na lastne stroške in vodi pisni obračun dni, ko jo je uporabljal. Stvar se vrne cela, najemodajalec pa je pred iztekom roka iz nobenega razloga ne vzame nazaj, ker je to bistvo roka. Izviri se vrnejo celi, ko rok poteče, obračun pa pove, kako.

Stolpec je naslovila NAJEM in podčrtala iz nobenega razloga.

IlluminaraVaš stolpec in moj se ujemata pri semenu, čolnu in tabli z imeni. Tudi najemnik popravi šiv in vreže črto na tablo.

Ines CalderPotem nam vaši predmeti ne morejo povedati ničesar.

IlluminaraPovedo nam lahko, ali skrbniki prepoznajo lastna pravila. Ne morejo nam povedati, kje se razidemo, razidemo pa se na enem mestu. Ali lahko posojilodajalec stvar pred iztekom roka pokliče domov, če jo potrebuje?

Calder je za hip molčala. Nato je naredila nekaj, česar Illuminara ni zahtevala, in izbrala primer.

Ines CalderZaporna loputa iz urada zbiralnika, posojena za čas obravnave. Sredi roka jo posojilodajalec pokliče nazaj. Dvakrat: enkrat, ker voda narašča, drugič brez kakršnegakoli razloga. In sodnik ne bo eden od vaših treh skrbnikov, ki so slišali vašo tabelo. Brann Crowe. Njegova družina ima trajekt že dvesto let in nima razloga, da bi vas imela rada.

Maren Tolliver, geodetka družbe, ki je enajst let prehodila Greben devet, je pristala, da bo vračala stvari. Vprašala je samo eno.

Maren TolliverKdo odloči, ali sem ravnala prav?

IlluminaraNe Ilo. Če bo to slonelo na enem starcu, bo spet samo navedek. Vsak skrbnik odloči za stvar, za katero skrbi, gospod Crowe pa za zaporno loputo. Če sodnik ne more odločiti, se primer šteje za nerešenega in meni ne koristi.

Ob 07:52 je svoje napovedi zapisala na kartico, Wren pa se je podpisala čez zavihek. Posojilni protokol bi zaključil oba odpoklica; najemniški ne bi zaključil nobenega. Pod njiju je zapisala vrstico, za katero je hotela, da jo Calder vidi: Če gospod Crowe najemniško zadržanje potrdi tudi ob poplavi, umaknem zahtevek glede odpoklica, družba pa lahko razstreli Greben devet in za izvire odgovarja v knjigi ob koncu roka. Če ga potrdi le ob muhi, zahtevek zožim na poplavo. Vse na grebenu je bilo odvisno od te kartice. Izvira, ki bi bil poškodovan v tretjem letu, v desetem ne bi bilo mogoče vrniti celega.

Ob 09:15 je Tolliver prevzela predmete. Wren je zapisala minuto, ko je posejala dva pladnja kreše, enega v prsti z grebena in drugega v prsti iz doline. Oseminštirideset ur, je rekla Teodora, je ena sezona kreše.

04 · Roke geodetke

Semenska hiša v Upper Haddowu · Šesti dan, 10:00

Laneno platno je delilo semensko hišo, nizko v njem pa je bila izrezana reža, skozi katero so se videle samo roke in predmet v njih. Na eni strani so za ločenimi mizami sedeli Teodora, Hamid in Anke, vsak s svinčnikom ter karticama ZAKLJUČENO in NI ZAKLJUČENO, za četrto mizo pa suh in brez nasmeha Brann Crowe. Na drugi strani je stala Maren Tolliver z zavihanimi rokavi, ob meri semena, čolnu in borovi tabli z devetimi vrezanimi imeni pa Ilo Marrow. Od setve je minilo oseminštirideset ur in petinštirideset minut.

Ilo je vsakič v jeziku Irú povedal kratek stavek predmetu, ne ženski, Illuminara pa je zapisala le čas. Tolliver je naredila, kar je pisalo na listu v njeni roki, in ni vedela, kateri protokol sledi.

Po najemniškem protokolu se je seme vrnilo celo, mera za mero, Teodora pa je označila ZAKLJUČENO. Po posojilnem se je vrnilo s prgiščem več in s stranjo o kalitvi, pladenj s prstjo z grebena siv od gnilobe ob zelenem pladnju iz doline, Teodora pa je tudi tega označila ZAKLJUČENO. Pri podelitvi je Tolliver obdržala mero in domov poslala eno seme, Teodora pa kartice sploh ni obrnila. Enako se je zgodilo s čolnom, pri podelitvi pa se je vrnil en sam žebelj, ki ga je Hamid s kazalcem porinil nazaj skozi režo. Pri tabli z imeni je Tolliver v borovino vrezala vrstico obračuna, Ilo pa je tabli govoril dlje, kot je zahtevala formula, tiho, z glasom, ki ni bil namenjen prostoru. Illuminara je zapisala neprevedeno, Ilo tabli in nič drugega.

Wren OdiraKaj je rekel?

IlluminaraČlovek je govoril tabli. Iz tega ne bom naredila nečesa, kar je povedal meni.

Anke je ob podelitev zapisala vprašaj. To je bila edina odločitev, ki je skrbniki niso mogli sprejeti, in Illuminara jo je vpisala kot nerešeno.

Ob 11:30 je sodni sluga skozi režo podal obvestilo, napisano s Hamidovo roko. Voda narašča. Zapornica potrebuje svojo loputo. Po posojilnem protokolu je Tolliver vrnila loputo z dnevnikom dni uporabe, Brann Crowe, ki odkar je sedel, ni rekel ničesar, pa je označil ZAKLJUČENO. Po najemniškem je rekla, da rok traja do desetega dne, in ponudila plačilo za izgubljene dni. Crowe je dolgo gledal loputo in označil NI ZAKLJUČENO.

Ob 12:10 je skozi režo prišlo drugo obvestilo. Posojilodajalec jo hoče nazaj. Nič več. Tolliver je loputo takoj vrnila, njene roke pa so se ob njej premikale počasi. Crowe je označil NI ZAKLJUČENO. Po najemniškem protokolu jo je zadržala do izteka roka, on pa je označil ZAKLJUČENO.

Wren je ob enih odprla ovojnico. Dve od štirih Illuminarinih oznak odpoklica sta bili napačni.

Ines CalderTorej je najem. Najem vzdrži muho.

Brann CroweVzdrži muho. Ne vzdrži poplave. Moji ljudje trajekta nikoli niso poklicali nazaj, ker se je vedno vračal domov s polenom. Če bi ga kdo poklical brez razloga, bi mu povedal, kam naj si vtakne poleno.

Illuminara je iz svojega stolpca prečrtala pravico, da jo pokliče nazaj in nad to zapisala zaradi potrebe. Napako je vpisala kot napako. Napovedala je, da lahko posojilodajalec stvar pokliče domov. Primer je pokazal: zaradi potrebe, ne zaradi užitka.

Maren TolliverMoje roke so našle razliko, vendar ne tiste, ki sem jo pričakovala. Ko sem loputo držala do izteka roka, sem opravljala posel. Ko sem jo odložila, ker je voda narasla, sem plačevala dolg, za katerega nisem vedela, da ga imam. Zadržana do roka ali vrnjena zaradi potrebe, ki vam jo nekdo pokaže. Samo to so moje roke lahko ločile.

Ines CalderOd vas so zahtevali, da uprizorite besedo, ki je ne govorite.

Maren TolliverVprašali so me, kaj pošten človek naredi z izposojeno stvarjo. Štirje ljudje, ki se še nikoli niso srečali, so mi povedali, eden od njih pa je bil vaša priča. Za to nisem potrebovala jezika Irú.

05 · Suho rame

Sodišče Kessel Reach, razpravna dvorana dve · Deveti dan, 15:20

Sedmega dne je svet družbi ponudil Suho rame, golo skalno sedlo južno od grebena, z za tretjino revnejšo rudo, posojeno z isto besedo in enakimi pogoji obračuna. Lastni vrtalni vzorci Tolliver iz leta 2019 so že bili dokazni predmet devet, Calder pa je stopnjo potrdila do osme ure tistega večera. Če je ne bi, je pisalo v Wreninem zvezku, bi sodišče opoldne osmega dne razsodilo samo o grebenu.

Sodnik Anselm Rhee je bral štirideset minut. Rekel je, da prikaz ni slovar in da bo stavek Ila Marrowa tabli ostal v zapisniku nepreveden. Zadevo je razdelil na tri dele in povedal, kateri je kateri. Glede besede so imeli ladijska knjiga iz leta 1727, dovoljenje za trajekt iz leta 1794 in četrti člen enak okvir: kontinuiteta je bila dokazana. Glede obveznosti so praksa skrbnikov in oznake gospoda Crowa pokazale dolg obračuna in vrnitev stvari, spremenjene z uporabo. Glede odpoklica sta ga en sam vpis iz leta 1731 in oznake gospoda Crowa utemeljila zaradi potrebe, ne pa zaradi muhe; sodišče je sprejelo takšno razsodbo v negotovosti.

Nato je povedal, čemu je odločitev namenjena. Najem brez odpoklica je družbi Harrow & Vane dovoljeval razstreljevanje ves čas roka in obračun za izvire v knjigi ob koncu, ko bi obveznost iz četrtega člena, da se jih vrne cele, zapadla za poškodovan vodonosnik, ki ga ne bi mogla popraviti nobena knjiga. Posojilo, ki ga je mogoče odpoklicati zaradi potrebe, je dolini dovoljevalo, da izvire pokliče domov, dokler jih je še mogoče vrniti, spodnji izvir pa je padel na tretjino zimskega pretoka. Izviri so poklicali. Če bi gospod Crowe najemniško zadržanje potrdil tudi ob poplavi, bi sodišče odredilo le obračun, družba pa bi razstreljevala. Zahtevek družbe Harrow & Vane do Grebena devet se je vrnil dolini.

Ines CalderSvoji stranki sem svetovala, naj se ne pritoži. Roke naše geodetke so v zapisniku in sama sem zapisala naš stolpec. Prosimo le, naj bo obračun letni in odpoklic zaradi potrebe zapisan, da ne bo treba nikomur na nobeni strani ugibati, kaj beseda pomeni v slabem letu.

Na Suhem ramenu štiristo rudarskih delovnih mest nikoli ne bo nastalo. Oren Basque, govorec sveta, ki je hotel, da družba zapusti ves greben, je podpisal s tresočo se roko. Družini Vesper in Hale sta izgubili poletni pašnik na sedlu in odšli brez besede.

Z zadnjim sklepom je sodišče družbi naložilo financiranje šole. Ilo Marrow mu je odgovoril s svojega stola v skupnem jeziku, še preden je sodnik končal.

Ilo MarrowZa to ne bom plačan. Posodil ga bom. Devet ljudi, vsak vzame eno stvar, seme, čoln ali ime, in jo vrne spremenjeno.

Pell Ardent je sklep prebrala v zapisnik brez mape. Maren Tolliver je iz zadnjega dela dvorane vprašala, ali jo lahko štejejo med deveterico, in nihče se ni zasmejal.

Ob 16:04 je Ilo na sodnih stopnicah mero semena položil v roke najmlajši med njimi, sedemletni deklici Pii, in besedo izrekel njej, ne semenu. Pia je v jeziku Irú odgovorila glasno in napačno, starec pa se je smejal, dokler ni zakašljal.

Wren OdiraTo je drugi govorec.

IlluminaraTo je prvi. Potrebuje jih še devet, nato pa potrebujejo drug drugega.

Wren je zapisala čas. Beseda je dolgo imela enega govorca, do pomladi pa jih bo imela deset.
